body.input: You take a math class, the professor sort of teaches it to you the way they understand it. Some of the students in the class sort of like, they get it. They start to get the way of thinking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And they can actually do the problems that get put on the homework that the professor thinks are interesting and challenging ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But most of the students who don't kind of engage as deeply don't ever get. And we think, oh, that man must be brilliant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: He must have this special insight. But he must have some biological sort of bit that's different that makes him so that he or she could have that insight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But although I don't want to dismiss biological individual differences completely, I find it much more interesting to think about the possibility that it was that difference in the dinner table conversation at the Chomsky house

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: when he was growing up that made it so that he had that cast of mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah. And there's a few topics we talked about that kind of interconnect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Because I wonder, the better I get at certain things, we humans, the deeper we understand something, what are you starting to then miss about the rest of the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: We talked about David and his degenerative mind. And when you look in the mirror and wonder how different am I cognitively from the man I was a month ago, from the man I was a year ago?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Like what, you know, if I can, having thought about language, if I'm Chomsky for 10, 20 years, what am I no longer able to see?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: What is in my blind spot? And how big is that? And then to somehow be able to leap back out of your deep structure that you formed for yourself about thinking about the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: leap back and look at the big picture again, or jump out of your current way of thinking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And to be able to introspect, like what are the limitations of your mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: How is your mind less powerful than you used to be or more powerful or different powerful in different ways?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So that seems to be a difficult thing to do because we're living, we're looking at the world through the lens of our mind, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: To step outside and introspect is difficult, but it seems necessary if you want to make progress.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You know, one of the threads of psychological research that's always been very,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I don't know, important to me to be aware of is the idea that our explanations of our own behavior

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: aren't necessarily actually part of the causal process that caused that behavior to occur,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: or even valid observations of the set of constraints that led to the outcome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But they are post-hoc rationalizations that we can give based on information at our disposal about what might have contributed to the result that we came to when asked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so this is an idea that was introduced in a very important paper by Nisbet and Wilson about the limits on our ability to be aware of the factors that cause us to make the choices that we make.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I think it's something that we really ought to be much more cognizant of in general as human beings,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: is that our own insight into exactly why we hold the beliefs that we do and we hold the attitudes and make the choices and feel the feelings that we do is not something that we totally control or totally observe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it's subject to our culturally transmitted understanding of what it is that is the mode that we give to explain these things when asked to do so as much as it is about anything else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so even our ability to introspect and think we have access to our own thoughts is a product of culture and belief, you know, practice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So let me ask you the big question of advice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So you've lived an incredible life in terms of the ideas you've put out into the world, in terms of the trajectory you've taken through your career, through your life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: What advice would you give to young people today in high school and college about how to have a career or how to have a life they can be proud of?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Finding the thing that you are intrinsically motivated to engage with and then celebrating that discovery is what it's all about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: When I was in college, I struggled with that. I had thought I wanted to be a psychiatrist because I think I was interested in human psychology in high school.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And at that time, the only sort of information I had that had anything to do with the psyche was, you know, Freud and Eric Fromm and sort of popular psychiatry kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so, well, they were psychiatrists, right? So I had to be a psychiatrist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that meant I had to go to medical school. And I got to college and I find myself taking, you know, the first semester of a three quarter physics class and it was mechanics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And this was so far from what it was I was interested in. But it was also too early in the morning in the winter court semester.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So I never made it to the physics class. But I wondered about the rest of my freshman year and most of my sophomore year until I found myself in the midst of this situation where around me there was this big revolution happening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I was at Columbia University in 1968 and the Vietnam War is going on. Columbia is building a gym in Morningside Heights, which is part of Harlem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And people are thinking, oh, the big bad rich guys are stealing the parkland that belongs to the people of Harlem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And, you know, they're part of the military industrial complex, which is enslaving us and sending us all off to war in Vietnam.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so there was a big revolution that involved a confluence of black activism and, you know, SDS and social justice and the whole university blew up and got shut down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I got a chance to sort of think about why people were behaving the way they were in this context.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I, you know, I happened to have taken mathematical statistics. I happened to have been taking psychology that quarter, just Psych 1.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And somehow things in that space all ran together in my mind and got me really excited about asking questions about why people, what made certain people go into the buildings and not others and things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so suddenly I had a path forward that and I had just been wandering around aimlessly and at the different points in my career, you know, when I think, OK, well, should I take this class or should I just read that book about?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Some idea that I want to understand better, you know, or should I should I pursue the thing that excites me and interests me or should I, you know, meet some requirement?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You know, that's I always did the latter. So I ended up my my professors in psychology were.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I thought I was great. They wanted me to go to graduate school. They they nominated me for Phi Beta Kappa. And I went to the Phi Beta Kappa ceremony and this guy came up and said, oh, you Magna Summa.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I wasn't even getting honors based on my grades. They just happened to have thought I was interested enough in ideas to belong to Phi Beta Kappa.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So, I mean, would it be fair to say you kind of stumbled around a little bit through accidents of too early morning of classes and physics and so on until you discovered intrinsic motivation, as you mentioned.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And then that's it. It hooked you. And then you celebrate the fact that this happens to human beings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah. Like and what is it that made what I did intrinsically motivating to me? Well, that's interesting. And I don't know all the answers to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I don't think I want to I want anybody to think that you should be sort of in any way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I don't know, sanctimonious or anything about it. You know, it's like I really enjoyed doing statistical analysis of data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I really enjoyed running my own experiment, which was what I got a chance to do in the psychology department that chemistry and physics had never.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I never imagined that mere mortals would ever do an experiment in those sciences, except one that was in the textbook that you were told to do in lab class. But in psychology, we were already like even when I was taking psych one, it turned out we had our own rat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And we got to after two set experiments, we got to OK, do something you think of, you know, with your rat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So it's the opportunity to do it myself and to to bring together a certain set of things that that engaged me intrinsically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I think it has something to do with why certain people turn out to be, you know, profoundly amazing musical geniuses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Right. They get immersed in it at an early enough point and it just sort of gets into the fabric.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So my my little brother had intrinsic motivation for music as we witnessed when he discovered how to put records on the phonograph when he was like 13 months old and recognize which one he wanted to play, not because he could read the labels,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: because he could sort of see which ones had which scratches, which were the different, you know, oh, that's rapid ESPANOL.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that's, you know, and and and he enjoyed that that connected with them somehow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah. And there was something that it fed into. And you're extremely lucky if you have that and if you can nurture it and can let it grow and let it be be an important part of your life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah, those are those are the two things is like be attentive enough to to feel it when it comes like this is something special.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I mean, I don't know. For example, I really like tabular data like Excel sheets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I get it brings me a deep joy. I don't know how useful that is for anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But there's this this is what I'm talking. Exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So there's like a million, not a million, but there's a lot of things like that for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You have to hear that for yourself, like be like realize this is really joyful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But then the other part that you're mentioning, which is the nurture, is take time and stay with it, stay with it while and see where that takes you in life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah, and I think I think the the the motivational engagement results in the immersion that then creates the opportunity to obtain the expertise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So, you know, we could call it the Mozart effect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Right. I mean, when I think about Mozart, I think about, you know, the person who was born as the fourth member of the family string quartet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Right. And and they handed him the violin when he was six weeks old.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: All right. Start playing. You know, it's like and so the level of immersion there was was amazingly profound.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But hopefully he also had, you know, some something. Maybe this is where the more sort of the genetic part comes in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Sometimes I think, you know, something in him resonated to the music so that that the synergy of the combination of that was so powerful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So that's what I really considered to be the Mozart effect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's sort of the the synergy of something with with experience that that then results in the unique flowering of a particular, you know, mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So I know my siblings and I are all very different from each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: We've all gone in our own different directions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And, you know, I mentioned my younger brother, who was very musical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I had my other younger brother was like this amazing, like intuitive engineer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And my sister, one of my sisters was passionate about, you know, water conservation well before it was, you know, such a hugely important issue that it is today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So we all sort of somehow these find a different thing. And I don't I don't mean to say it isn't tied in with something about about us biologically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But but it's also when that happens, where you can find that, then, you know, you can do your thing and you can be excited about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So people can be excited about fitting people on bicycles, as well as excited about making neural networks achieve insights into human cognition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Right. Yeah. Like for me personally, I've always been excited about love and friendship between humans and just like the actual experience of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's as I was a child, just observing people around me and also been excited about robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And there's something in me that things I really would love to explore how those two things combine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it doesn't make any sense. A lot of it is also timing. Just to think of your own career and your own life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You found yourself in certain pieces, places that happen to involve some of the greatest thinkers of our time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so it just worked out that, like, you guys develop those ideas and there may be a lot of other people similar to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And they were brilliant. And they never found that right connection and place to where they the ideas could flourish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So it's timing, it's place, it's people. And ultimately the whole ride, you know, it's undirected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Can I ask you about something you mentioned in terms of psychiatry when you were younger?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Because I had a similar experience of, you know, reading Freud and Carl Jung and just, you know, those kind of popular psychiatry ideas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that was a dream for me early on in high school to, like, I hope to understand the human mind by...

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Somehow psychiatry felt like the right discipline for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Does that make you sad that psychiatry is not the mechanism by which you are able to explore the human mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So for me, I was a little bit disillusioned because of how much prescription medication and biochemistry is involved in the discipline of psychiatry,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: as opposed to the dream of the Freud, like, use the mechanisms of language to explore the human mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So that was a little disappointing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that's why I kind of went to computer science and thinking, like, maybe you can explore the human mind by trying to build the thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yes, I wasn't exposed to the sort of the biomedical slash pharmacological aspects of psychiatry at that point, because I didn't...

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I dropped out of that whole idea of pre-med that I never even found out about that until much later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But you're absolutely right. So I was actually a member of the National Advisory Mental Health Council,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that is to say the board of scientists who advise the director of the National Institute of Mental Health.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that was around the year 2000.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And in fact, at that time, the man who came in as the new director, I had been on this board for a year when he came in,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: said, okay, schizophrenia is a biological illness. It's a lot like cancer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: We've made huge strides in curing cancer. And that's what we're going to do with schizophrenia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: We're going to find the medications that are going to cure this disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And we're not going to listen to anybody's grandmother anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And good old behavioral psychology is not something we're going to support any further.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: He completely alienated me from the Institute and from all of its prior policies, which had been much more holistic, I think, really, at some level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And the other people on the board were like psychiatrists, right? Very biological psychiatrists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It didn't pan out, right? That nothing has changed in our ability to help people with mental illness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so 20 years later, that particular path was a dead end, as far as I can tell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Well, there's some aspect to and sorry to romanticize the whole philosophical conversation about the human mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But to me, psychiatrists for time held the flag of we're the deep thinkers in the same way that physicists are the deep thinkers about the nature of reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Psychiatrists are the deep thinkers about the nature of the human mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I think that flag has been taken from them and carried by people like you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's like it's more in the cognitive psychology, especially when you have a foot in the computational view of the world, because you can both build it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You can like intuit about the functioning of the mind by building little models and be able to see mathematical things and then deploying those models, especially in computers, to say, does this actually work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: They do like experiments and then some combination of neuroscience where you're starting to actually be able to observe, you know, do certain experience on human beings and observe how the brain is actually functioning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And they're using intuition. You can start being the philosopher like Richard Feynman is the philosopher.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Cognitive psychologists can become the philosopher and psychiatrists become much more like doctors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: They're like very medical. They help people with medication, biochemistry and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But they are no longer the the the book writers and the philosophers, which, of course, I admire.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I admire the Richard Feynman ability to do great low level mathematics and physics and the high level philosophy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah, I think it was from and young more than Freud that was sort of initially kind of like made me feel like, oh, this is really amazing and interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I want to explore it further.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I actually when I got to college and I lost that thread, I I found more of it in sociology and literature than I did in any place else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So I took quite a lot of both of those disciplines as an undergraduate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And, you know, I was actually deeply ambivalent about the psychology because I was doing experiments after the initial flurry of interest in why people would occupy buildings during a insurrection and consider, you know, be be sort of like so overcommitted to their beliefs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But I ended up in in the psychology laboratory running experiments on pigeons. And and so I had these profound sort of like dissonance between, OK, the kinds of issues that would be explored when I was thinking about what I read about in in modern British literature

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: versus what I could study with my pigeons in the laboratory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that got resolved when I went to graduate school and I discovered cognitive psychology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so for me, that was that was the path out of this sort of like extremely sort of ambivalent divergence between the interest in the human condition and the desire to do, you know, actual mechanistically oriented thinking about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I think we we've come a long way in that regard and that you're absolutely right that nowadays this is something that's accessible to people through the pathway in through computer science or the pathway in through neuroscience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You know, you can get derailed in neuroscience down to the bottom of the system where you might find the cures of various conditions, but you don't get a chance to think about the higher level stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So it's in the systems and cognitive neuroscience and computational intelligence, my asthma up there at the top that I think these opportunities are most are richest right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so, yes, I am indeed blessed by having had the opportunity to fall into that space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So you mentioned the human condition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Speaking of which, you happen to be a human being who's unfortunately not immortal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: That seems to be a fundamental part of the human condition that this riot ends.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Do you think about the fact that you're going to die one day? Are you afraid of death?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I would say that I am not as much afraid of death as I am of degeneration.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I say that in part for reasons of having, you know, seen some tragic degenerative situations unfold.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's exciting when you can continue to participate and feel like you're near the place where the wave is breaking on the shore, if you like, you know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I think about, you know, my own future potential.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: If I were to undergo a begin to suffer from dementia, Alzheimer's disease or some dementia or some other condition, you know, I would sort of gradually lose the thread of that ability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so one can live on for several, for a decade after, you know, sort of having to retire because one no longer has these kinds of abilities to engage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I think that's the thing that I fear the most.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: The losing of that, like the breaking of the wave, the flourishing of the mind where you have these ideas and they're swimming around, you're able to play with them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah. And collaborate with other people who, you know, are themselves really helping to push these ideas forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: What about the edge of the cliff? The end.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: The mystery of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: The migrated sort of conception of mind and, you know, sort of continuous sort of way of thinking about most things makes it so that to me the discreteness of that transition is less apparent than it seems to be to most people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I see. I see. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I wonder, so I don't know if you know the work of Ernest Becker and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I wonder what role mortality and our ability to be cognizant of it and anticipate it and perhaps be afraid of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: What role that plays in our understanding of the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I think that it can be motivating to people to think they have a limited period left.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I think in my own case, you know, it's like seven or eight years ago now that I was sitting around doing experiments on decision making that were satisfying in a certain way because I could really get closure on whether the model fit the data perfectly or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I could see how one could test, you know, the predictions in monkeys as well as humans and really see what the neurons were doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But I just realized, hey, wait a minute, you know, I may only have about 10 or 15 years left here and I don't feel like I'm getting towards the answers to the really interesting questions while I'm doing this this particular level of work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that's when I said to myself, OK, let's pick something that's hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So that's when I started working on mathematical cognition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I think it was more in terms of, well, I got 15 more years possibly of useful life left.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Let's imagine that it's only 10.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I'm actually getting close to the end of that now, maybe three or four more years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But I'm beginning to feel like, well, I probably have another five after that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So, OK, I give myself another another six or eight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But a deadline is looming and therefore going to go on forever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so so yeah, I got to keep thinking about the questions that I think are the interesting and important ones for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: What do you hope your legacy is?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You've done some incredible work in your life as a man, as a scientist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: When the aliens and the human civilization is long gone and the aliens are reading the encyclopedia about the human species, what do you hope is the paragraph written about you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I would want it to sort of highlight a couple of things that I was able to see one path

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that was more exciting to me than the one that seemed already to be there for a cognitive psychologist, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: but not for any super special reason other than that I'd had the right context prior to that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: but that I had gone ahead and followed that lead, you know, and then I forget the exact wording.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But I said in this preface that the joy of science is the moment in which, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: a partially formed thought in the mind of one person gets crystallized a little better in the discourse

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and becomes the foundation of some exciting concrete piece of actual scientific progress.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I feel like that, you know, moment happened when Rumelhart and I were doing the interactive activation model

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: and when Rumelhart heard Hinton talk about gradient descent and having the objective function to guide the learning process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it happened a lot in that period and I sort of seek that kind of thing in my collaborations with my students, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So, you know, the idea that this is a person who contributed to science by finding exciting collaborative opportunities

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: to engage with other people through is something that I certainly hope is part of the paragraph.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And like you said, taking a step maybe in directions that are non-obvious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So it's the old Robert Frost road less taken.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So maybe because you said like this incomplete initial idea, that step you take is a little bit off the beaten path.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: If I could just say one more thing here, this was something that really contributed to energizing me in a way that I feel it would be useful to share.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: My PhD dissertation project was completely empirical experimental project.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I wrote a paper based on the two main experiments that were the core of my dissertation and I submitted it to a journal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And at the end of the paper, I had a little section where I laid out the beginnings of my theory about what I thought was going on

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: that would explain the data that I had collected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I had submitted the paper to the Journal of Experimental Psychology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So I got back a letter from the editor saying, thank you very much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: These are great experiments and we'd love to publish them in the journal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But what we'd like you to do is to leave the theorizing to the theorists and take that part out of the paper.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so I did. I took that part out of the paper.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But I almost found myself labeled as a non-theorist by this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I could have succumbed to that and said, okay, well, I guess my job is to just go on and do experiments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But that's not what I wanted to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so when I got to my assistant professorship, although I continued to do experiments because I knew I had to get some papers out,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I also at the end of my first year submitted my first article to Psychological Review,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: which was the theoretical journal where I took that section and elaborated it and wrote it up and submitted it to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And they didn't accept that either.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But they said, oh, this is interesting. You should keep thinking about it this time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And then that was what got me going to think, okay, you know, so it's not a superhuman thing to contribute to the development of theory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You know, you don't have to be. You can do it as a mere mortal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And the broader, I think, lessons don't succumb to the labels of a particular reviewer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Or anybody labeling you, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Exactly. I mean, yeah, exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And especially as you become successful, labels get assigned to you for that you're successful for that thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I'm a connectionist or a cognitive scientist and not a neuroscientist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And then you can completely. That's just that's the stories of the past.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You're today a new person that can completely revolutionize in totally new areas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So don't let those labels hold you back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Well, let me ask the big question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: When you look at into the you said it started with Colombia trying to observe these humans and they're doing weird stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And you want to know why are they doing this stuff?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So zoom out even bigger at the 100 plus billion people who've ever lived on Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Why do you think we're all doing what we're doing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: What do you think is the meaning of it all? The big why question?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: We seem to be very busy doing a bunch of stuff and we seem to be kind of directed towards somewhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But why?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Well, I myself think that we make meaning for ourselves and that we find inspiration in the meaning that other people have made in the past.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You know, and the great religious thinkers of the first millennium B.C.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And, you know, few few that came in the early part of the second millennium, you know, laid down some important foundations for us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But I do believe that, you know, we are an emergent result of a process that happened naturally without guidance and that meaning is what we make of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And that the creation of efforts to reify meaning in like religious traditions and so on is just a part of the expression of that of that goal that we have to, you know, not not find out what the meaning is, but to make it ourselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And so to me, it's something that's very personal. It's very individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's like meaning will come for you through the particular combination of synergistic elements that are your fabric and your experience and your context.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And, you know, you should.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's all made in a certain kind of a local context, though, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: What here I am at UCSD with this brilliant man, Rommelhart, who's having, you know, these doubts about symbolic artificial intelligence that resonate with my desire to see it grounded in the biology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And let's make the most of that, you know?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Yeah. And so and so from that, like little pocket, there's some kind of peculiar little emergent process that then which is basically each one of us, each one of us humans is a kind of, you know, you think cells and they come together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And it's an emergent process that then tells fancy stories about itself and then gets just like you said, just enjoys the beauty of the stories we tell about ourselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's an emergent process that lives for time, is defined by its local pocket and context in time and space and then tells pretty stories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And we write those stories down and then we celebrate how nice the stories are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And then it continues because we build stories on top of each other and eventually will colonize, hopefully other planets, other solar systems, other galaxies, and will tell even better stories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: But all starts here on Earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Jay, you're speaking of peculiar emergent processes that lived one heck of a story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You're you're one of the great scientists of cognitive science, of psychology, of computation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: It's a huge honor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: You talked to me today that you spend your very valuable time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I really enjoyed talking with you and thank you for all the work you've done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: I can't wait to see what you do next.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: Well, thank you so much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: And I know this has been an amazing opportunity for me to let ideas that I've never fully expressed before come out because you asked such a wide range of, you know, the deeper questions that we're all we've all been thinking about for so long.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jay McClelland: Neural Networks and the Emergence of Cognition | Lex Fridman Podcast #222

body.input: So thank you very much for that.
