metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and I just am happy as a cow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And I wake up after all the drama has been resolved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And cows are happy and the drama has been resolved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But in society you do, especially,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I mean this is what I think about is

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: when you work on a larger team, especially with companies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: you are, everybody's awake at the same time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So that's definitely been a struggle to try to figure out,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: just like you said, how to balance that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: how to fit into society and yet be optimal

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: for your chronotype.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: You said, yup.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: You have to sleep in synchrony with it and harmony.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Because normally what we know is that if you fight biology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: you'll normally lose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And the way you know you've lost is

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: through disease and sickness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: You said you suffered through several bouts of insomnia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Is there, aside from embracing your chronotype,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: is there advice you can give how to overcome insomnia

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: from your own experience?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Right now the best method that we have

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: is something called cognitive behavioral therapy

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: for insomnia or CBTI for short.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And you work with, for people who don't know what it is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: you work with a therapist for maybe six weeks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And you can do it online, by the way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I would recommend probably jumping online,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: it's just the easiest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And it will change your beliefs, your habits,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: your behaviors and your general stress

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: around this thing called sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And it is just as effective as sleeping pills

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: in the short term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But what's great is that unlike sleeping pills,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: when you stop working with your therapist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: those benefits last for years later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Whereas when you stop your sleeping pills,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: you typically have what's called rebound insomnia,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: where your sleep not only goes back

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: to being as bad as it was before,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: it's usually even worse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: For me, I think I found a number of things effective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: The first is that I had to really address

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: what was stressful and try to come up with

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: some degree of meaningful rationality around it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Because I think one of the things that happens,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: there's something very, talking about conscious states,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: to come all the way back to, gosh, I don't know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I feel like we've only been chatting for like 20 minutes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but you're gonna tell me it's been a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Yeah, it's been a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Okay, I'm desperately, I feel terribly sorry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But let's get back to conscious states,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: where we started.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: There is something very strange about the night,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that thoughts and anxieties are not the same as they are

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: in the waking day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: They are worse, they are bigger.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And I at least find that I am far more likely

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: to catastrophize and ruminate at night about things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that when I wake up the next day in the broad light of day,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I think it's nowhere near that bad man.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: What were you doing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's not that bad at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So to gain firstly, some rational understanding

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: of my emotional state that's causing that insomnia

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: was very helpful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: The second thing was to keep regularity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: just going to bed at the same time waking up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And here's an unconventional piece of sleep advice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: After a bad night of sleep, do nothing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Don't think, don't wake up any later,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: don't go to bed any earlier, don't nap during the day,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and don't drink any more coffee than you would otherwise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Because if you end up sleeping later into the morning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: you're then not going to be tired

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: at your normal time at night.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So then you're gonna get into bed thinking,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: well, I had a terrible night of sleep last night.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And yes, I slept in this morning to try and compensate,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but I'm still gonna get to bed at my normal time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But now you get into bed and you haven't been awake

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: for as long as you normally would.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So you're not as sleepy as you normally would be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And so now you sit there lying in bed

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and it's another bad night.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And the same thing is, if you go to bed any earlier,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: so don't wake up any later, wake up at the same time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: don't go to bed any earlier,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: because then you're just probably your chronotype,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: your biological rhythm doesn't want you to be asleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And you think, well, terrible night,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I'm gonna get into bed at 9 p.m. rather than my standard 10.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: You're just gonna be lying in bed awake for that hour.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Naps will take our double-edged sword.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: They can have wonderful benefits.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And we've done lots of studies on naps

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: for both the brain and the body.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But they are a double-edged sword in the sense that

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: napping will just take the edge off your sleepiness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's a little bit like a valve on a pressure cooker.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: When you nap during the day,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: you can take some of that healthy sleepiness

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that you've been building up during the day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And for some people, not all people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but for some people that can then make it harder

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: for them to fall asleep at night

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and then stay asleep soundly across the night.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So the advice would be,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: if you're struggling with sleep at night,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: don't nap during the day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But if you are not struggling with sleep

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and you can nap regularly, naps are just fine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And we can play around with optimal durations

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: depending on what you want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Just try not to nap too late into the day

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: because napping late into the day

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: is like snacking before your main meal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It just takes the edge off your sleep hunger, as it were.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But that would be,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: so that's my unconventional second piece of advice

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: regarding insomnia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: The third is meditation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I found meditation to be incredibly powerful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I started reading about meditation

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: as I was researching that aspect of the book many years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And as a hard-nosed scientist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I thought this sounds very woo-woo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: This is sort of, we all hold hands and sing Kumbhaya

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and everything's going to be fine with sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I read the data and it was compelling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I couldn't ignore it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And I started meditating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And that was six years ago and I haven't stopped.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And I found meditation before bed incredibly powerful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: The meditation app companies were perplexed at this at first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: They want people to meditate during the day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But when they looked at their usage statistics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: they found that they would have people in the morning

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: meditating and then there's a huge number of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: using the meditation app in the evening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: What they were doing was self-medicating their insomnia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And they finally, rather than railing against it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: they started to see it as a cash cow, rightly so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So I found meditation to be helpful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Having a wind down routine

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: is the other thing that's critical for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I can't just go from,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: because when my mind is switched on

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and I think you may be like this too,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: if I get into bed,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that Rolodex of thoughts and information and excitement

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and anxiety and worry is just whirling away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And it's not gonna be a good night for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So I have to find a wind down routine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And that makes sense when you realize what sleep is like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Sleep is not like a light switch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Sleep is much more like trying to land a plane.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It takes time to descend down onto the terra firma

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that we call sound sleep at night.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And we have this for kids.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I don't have children,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So I do intermittent fasting sometimes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: only one meal a day, sometimes no meals a day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Is there a good science on the interaction

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: between fasting and sleep?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: We have some data, I would prefer more,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but we have data both on time restricted eating

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and then we have some data on fasting to a degree.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: On time restricted eating,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I think that it has some benefits,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: although the human replication studies

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: have actually not borne out quite the same health benefit

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: extent that the animal studies have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: There've been some disappointing studies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: one here close to where we are right now at UCSF recently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So I think time restricted eating can be a good thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and there are many benefits of time restricted eating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Is sleep one of them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: No, it doesn't seem to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Because there are probably at the time

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that we're recording this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: three pretty decent studies that I'm aware of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Two out of the three were in obese individuals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: one out of the three were in healthy weight individuals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And what they found was that time restricted eating

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: in all three of those studies

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: didn't have any advantageous benefit to sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It didn't necessarily harm sleep,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but it didn't seem to improve it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: When it comes to fasting though, which is a different state,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: we don't have too many experimental studies

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: with long-term fasting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: The best data that we have is probably

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: from religious practices.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And probably the most data we have is during Ramadan

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: where people will fast for 29 to 30 days

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: from sunrise to sunset.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And under those conditions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: there are probably five distinct changes that we've seen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: None of them seem to be particularly good for sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: The first is that the amount of melatonin

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that you release, and melatonin is a hormone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's often called the hormone of darkness

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: or the vampire hormone,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: not because it makes you look longingly

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: at people's necklines,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but it's just because it comes out at night.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Melatonin signals to your brain that, and your body,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that it's dark, it's nighttime, and it's time to sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Those individuals, when they were undergoing

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that regimen to fasting,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: the amount of melatonin that was released

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and when it was released,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: the amount of melatonin decreased,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and when it was released came later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: That was the first thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: The second thing was that they ended up finding it harder

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: to fall asleep as quickly as they normally would otherwise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: The third thing was that the total amount of sleep

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that they were getting decreased.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: The fourth fascinating thing was that a wake promoting

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: chemical called orexin increased.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And this is why a lot of people will say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: when I'm fasting, it feels like I can stay awake for longer

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and I'm more alert, I'm more active.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And I'll come back from an evolutionary perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: why we understand that to be the case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And then the fourth factor is that fasting didn't decrease

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: the amount of deep sleep that seemed to be unaffected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It did, however, decrease the amount of REM sleep

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: or dream sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And we know that REM sleep dreaming is essential

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: for emotional first aid, mental health.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's critical for memory, creativity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's also critical for several hormone functions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's when, you know, if you, there's direct correlations

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: between testosterone, you know, testosterone release peaks

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: just before you go into REM sleep and during REM sleep too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So REM sleep is critical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But so those are the five changes that we've seen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: None of them seem to be that advantageous for sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But the fourth point that I mentioned, which was orexin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: which is this wake promoting chemical,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and a good demonstration or a very sad demonstration

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: of its power is when it becomes very deficient in the brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and it leads to a condition called narcolepsy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: where, you know, you're just unpredictable

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: with your sleep and you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So, so orexin when it's in high concentrations

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: keeps you awake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: When you lose it, it can, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: it can put you very much into a state of narcolepsy

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: where you're sleeping a lot of the time

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: in unpredictable sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Why on earth when you are fasting

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: would the brain release a wake promoting chemical?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And our answer is right now is the following.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: One of the few times that I mentioned before

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that we see animals undergoing insufficient sleep

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: or prolonged sleep deprivation

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: is under conditions of starvation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And that is an extreme evolutionary pressure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And at that point, the brain will forgo some,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: it won't forgo all, but it will forgo some of its sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And the reason is so that it can stay awake for longer

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: because the sign of starvation is saying to the brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: you can't find food in your normal foraging perimeter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: You need to stay awake for longer

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: so you can travel outside of your perimeter

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: for a further distance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And maybe you will find food and save the organism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So in other words, when we fast,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: it's giving our brain this evolutionary signal

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that you are under conditions of starvation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So the brain responds by saying, oh my goodness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I need to release the chemical

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that helps the organism stay awake for longer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: which is a rexin, so that they can forage for more food.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Now, of course, your brain from revolutionary perspective

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: doesn't know about this thing called Safeway

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that you could easily go to and break the fast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But that's how we understand fasting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And I think my dear friend, Peter Tia,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: has done a lot of work in this area too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I think fasting and David Sinclair's brilliant work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: goodness me, what an individual too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: The work is pretty clear there that time restricted eating

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and fasting have wonderful health benefits.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Fasting creates this thing called hermesis,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: just like exercise and low level stress

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and sauna, heat, shock.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And hermesis is a biological process,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I think as David Sinclair has once said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: in simple layman's terms is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: what doesn't kill you makes you stronger.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And I think there is certainly good data

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that fasting and time restricted eating has many benefits.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Is sleep one of them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It doesn't seem to be, it doesn't seem to enhance sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But it's interesting to understand its effects on sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I've like, I've fasted,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: it's a study of NF2.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I once fasted 72 hours and another time 48 hours.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And I found that I got much less sleep

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and it was very restful though.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I hesitate to say this, but this is how I felt,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: which is I needed less sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I wonder if my brain is deceiving me

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: because it feels like I'm getting a whole extra amount

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: of focus for free.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And I wonder if there's long-term impacts of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Because if I fast 24 hours,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: get the same amount of calories, one meal a day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: There's a little bit of discomfort,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: like just maybe your body gets a little bit colder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Maybe there's just, I mean, you, hunger.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But the amount of focus is crazy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And so I wonder, it's like, I'm a little suspicious of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I feel like I'm getting something for free.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I'm the same way with sweetener, like Splendor or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's like, it's gotta be really bad for you, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Because why is it so tasty?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And I think, yeah, as we said before with biology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: if there's a gain, there's often a cost too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So, but we are at least understand the biological basis

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: of what you're describing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's not that you actually don't need less sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's that this chemical is present

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that forces you more awake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And so subjectively you feel as though

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I don't need as much sleep because I'm wide awake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And those two things are quite different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's not as though your sleep need has decreased.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's that your brain has hit the overdrive switch,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: the overboost switch to say, we need to keep you awake

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: because food is in short supply.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So you mentioned during sleep, there's a simulation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: all those kinds of things for learning purposes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but there's also these, and you mentioned the five ways

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: in which we become psychotic in dreams.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: What do you think dreams are about?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: What, why do you think we dream?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: What place do we go to when we dream?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And why are they useful?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Not just the assimilation aspect,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but just like all the crazy visuals that we get with dreams.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Is there something you can speak to that's actually useful?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Like why we have such fun experiences in that dream world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So one of the camps in the sleep field

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: is that dreams are meaningless,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that they are an epiphenomenal byproduct

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: of this thing called REM sleep from which dreams come from

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: as a physiological state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So the analogy would be, let's think of a light bulb,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that the reason that you create the apparatus of a light bulb

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: is to produce this thing called light

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: in the same way that we've evolved

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: to this thing called REM sleep

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: to serve whatever functions REM sleep serves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But it turns out that when you create light in that way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: you also produce something called heat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It was never the reason that you designed the light bulb,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: it's just what happens when you create light in that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And the belief so too was that dreaming

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: was essentially the heat of the light bulb,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that REM sleep is critical,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but when you have REM sleep with a complex brain like ours,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: you also produce this conscious epiphenomenon

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: called dreaming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I don't believe that for a second.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And from a simple perspective is that I suspect

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that dreaming is more metabolically costly

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: as a conscious experience than not dreaming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So you could still have REM sleep,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but absent the conscious experience of dreaming

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: was probably less metabolically costly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And whenever mother nature burns the energy unit called ATP,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: which is the most valuable thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: there's usually a reason for it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So if it's more energetically demanding,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: then I suspect that there is a function to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And we've now since discovered that dreams have a function.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: The first, as we mentioned, creativity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: The second is that dreams provide a form

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: of overnight therapy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Dreaming is a form of emotional first aid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And it's during dream sleep at night

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that we take these dreams to sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: We take these difficult, painful experiences

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that we've had during the day, sometimes traumatic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And dream sleep acts almost like a nocturnal soothing balm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And it sort of just takes the sharp edges

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: off those difficult, painful experiences

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: so that you come back the next day

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and you feel better about them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And so I think in that sense, dreaming,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: it's not time that heals all wounds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's time during dream sleep

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that provides emotional convalescence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So dreaming is almost a form of emotional windscreen wipers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And I think, and by the way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: it's not just that you dream,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: it's what you dream about that also matters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So for example, scientists have done studies

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: with learning in memory where they have people

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: learn a virtual maze.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And what they discovered was that those people

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: who then dreamed, but dreamed of the maze

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: were the only ones who, when they woke up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: ended up being better at navigating the maze.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Whereas those people who dreamed,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but didn't dream about the maze itself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: they were no better at navigating the maze.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So it's not just that you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: it's not sort of necessary, but not sufficient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's necessary that you dream,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but it's not sufficient to produce the benefit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: You have to be dreaming about certain things itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And the same is true for mental health.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: What we've discovered is that people

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: who are going through a very difficult experience,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: a trauma, for example, a very painful divorce,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: those people who are dreaming,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but dreaming of that difficult event itself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: they go on to gain resolution

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: to their clinical depression one year later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Whereas people who were dreaming just as much,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but not dreaming about the trauma itself

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: did not go on to gain as much clinical resolution

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: to their depression.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So it's, I think to me, those are the lines of evidence

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that tell me dreaming is not epiphenomenal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And it's not just about the act of dreaming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's about the content of the dreams,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: not just the fact of a dream itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's, first of all, it's fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It makes a lot of sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but then immediately takes my mind to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: from an engineering perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: how that could be useful in, for example, AI systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: If you think about dreaming as an important part

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: about learning and cognition

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: as if it's chemically brute forced

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: into this relaxed associative memory processing state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And then from an anatomical perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: just as I described,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: the prefrontal cortex goes down

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and other regions light up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So it is a state that seems to be very,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I mean, if you were to show me a brain scan of REM sleep

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and tell me that it's not REM sleep,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: just say, look, based on the pattern of this brain activity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: what would you say is going on in this person's mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I would say, well, they're probably not rational.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: They're probably not having logical thought

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: because their prefrontal cortex is down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: They're probably feeling very emotional

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: because their amygdala is active,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: which is an emotional center of the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: They're definitely going to be thinking visually

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: because the back of the brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: has lit up the visual cortex.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's probably going to be filled with past experience

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and autobiographical memories

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: because their memory centers are lighting up

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and there's probably going to be movement

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: because their motor cortex is very active.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: That to me sounds very much like a dream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And that's exactly what we see in brain scanners

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: when we've put people inside of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: One of the things I notice sleep effects

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: is my ability to see the beauty in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So what do you think is the connection

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: between sleep and your emotional life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: your ability to love other human beings and love life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I think it's very powerful and strong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So we've done a lot of work in the field of sleep

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and emotion and sleep and moods,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and you can separate your emotions into two main buckets,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: positive and negative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And what's interesting is that when you are sleep deprived

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and the more hours that you go into being awake

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: and the fewer hours that you've had to sleep,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: your negative mood starts to increase.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And we know which individual types of emotions are changing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I've got a wonderful postdoc in my lab called

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Eddie Ben Simon, who's doing some incredible work

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: on trying to understand the emotional,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: individual emotional tapestry of affective meltdown

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: when you're not getting sufficient sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But let's just keep with two dimensions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: positive and negative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: The negative, most people would think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: well, it's the negative that takes the biggest hit

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: when I'm sleep deprived.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's not by probably a log order magnitude larger

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: is a hit on your positive emotions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: In other words, you stop gaining pleasure

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: from normally pleasurable things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And it's a state that we call anhedonia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And anhedonia is the state that we often call depression.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: So depression to most people's surprise

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: isn't necessarily that you're always feeling negative emotions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: It's often more about the fact that you lose the pleasure

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: in the good things in life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: That's what we call anhedonia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: That's what we see in sleep and insufficient sleep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: And it happens quite quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Yeah, it's kind of fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I think I do, it's not depression,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: but like it's a stroll into that direction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: which is when I'm sleep deprived,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I stop being able to see the meaning in life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: The things that gave me meanings starts to lose meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Like stupid, it makes me realize

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: how enjoyable everything is in my life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: Because when I start to lose it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: when I'm severely sleep deprived,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: you start to see how much life sucks when you lose it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: But that said, I'm just cognizant enough

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: that like sleep fixes all of that.

body.input: So I use those states for what they're worth.

body.input: to the things that bother me in doing that time.

body.input: Because they also reveal important information to me.

body.input: Yeah, it's an interesting method.

body.input: Use like a raw shock to-

body.input: Yeah, I mean, there's, so I find this

body.input: when I fast combined with sleep deprivation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: am clear to see with people,

body.input: in my life or people that I'm working with

metadata.title: Podcast: Matt Walker: Sleep | Lex Fridman Podcast #210

body.input: I'm more able to identify them.

body.input: I'm like recording that information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: Let's start with the most absurd question, but I've read you write some fascinating stuff about it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: so let's go there. Are we living in a simulation? What difference does it make, Lex? I mean, I'm

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: serious. What difference? Because if we are living in a simulation, it raises the question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: how real does something have to be in simulation for it to be sufficiently immersive?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: But I mean, even in principle, how could we ever know if we were in one, right? A perfect simulation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: by definition, is something that's indistinguishable from the real thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: But we didn't say anything about perfect. It could be imperfect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: No, no, that's right. Well, if it was an imperfect simulation, if we could hack it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: find a bug in it, then that would be one thing, right? If this was like The Matrix and there was

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: a way for me to do flying kung fu moves or something by hacking this in, then it would be

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: like we would have to cross that bridge when we came to it, wouldn't we? I mean, at that point,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: it's hard to see the difference between that and just what people would ordinarily refer to as a

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: world with miracles. What about from a different perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: thinking about the universe as a computation, like a program running on a computer. That's kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: a neighboring concept. It is an interesting and reasonably well-defined question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: It's an interesting and reasonably well-defined question to ask, is the world computable?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: Does the world satisfy what we would call in CS the church touring thesis? That is, could we take

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: any physical system and simulate it to any desired precision by a touring machine, given

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: the appropriate input data, right? And so far, I think the indications are pretty strong that

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: our world does seem to satisfy the church touring thesis. At least if it doesn't, then we haven't

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: yet discovered why not. But now, does that mean that our universe is a simulation? Well, that

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: word seems to suggest that there is some other larger universe in which it is running, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: And the problem there is that if the simulation is perfect, then we're never going to be able

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: to get any direct evidence about that other universe. We will only be able to see the effects

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: of the computation that is running in this universe. Well, let's imagine an analogy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: Let's imagine a PC, a personal computer, a computer. Is it possible with the advent of

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: artificial intelligence for the computer to look outside of itself to understand its creator?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: Mm-hmm. I mean, is that a ridiculous connect analogy?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: Well, I mean, with the computers that we actually have, I mean, first of all, we all know that

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: humans have done an imperfect job of enforcing the abstraction boundaries of computers, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: Like you may try to confine some program to a playpen, but as soon as there's one

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: memory allocation error in the C program, then the program has gotten out of that playpen and it can

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: do whatever it wants, right? This is how most hacks work, you know, viruses and worms and exploits.

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: And you would have to imagine that an AI would be able to discover something like that. Now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: of course, if we could actually discover some exploit of reality itself, then this whole,

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: I mean, then in some sense, we wouldn't have to philosophize about this, right? This would no

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: longer be a metaphysical conversation. Well, this was just the...

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: But the question is, what would that hack look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: Yeah, well, I have no idea. I mean, Peter Shor, the very famous person in quantum computing,

body.input: of course, has a joke that maybe the reason why we haven't yet integrated general relativity

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: more physics, not necessarily the unification of the laws, but just understand physics more deeply

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130

body.input: at the fundamental level, we'll be able to start, you know, I mean, part of this is humorous, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Scott Aaronson: Computational Complexity and Consciousness | Lex Fridman Podcast #130
