body.input: The following is a conversation with Michael Mina, his second time on the podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: He's a professor at Harvard doing research on infectious disease and immunology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: In my view, the most powerful, doable, and obvious solution to COVID-19 from the very beginning

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: is rapid at-home testing. This is what Michael has been talking about and writing about since

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: the beginning of the pandemic. The accuracy of these tests is high for the task of detecting

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: contagiousness, which is what matters. Hundreds of millions can be manufactured quickly and

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: relatively cheaply. Privacy and individual freedoms are preserved. I believe that if you give people

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: the power of information, information about whether they are contagious or not, they will

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: do the right thing, at scale, all while respecting their freedom and minimizing the destructive

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: effects of the pandemic on our health and our economy. This solution was obvious in May of 2020.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: It was obvious when Michael and I spoke the first time a year ago, and it is obvious today. We talk

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: about why it has not yet been done and how we can still do it. This is the Lex Friedman Podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: To support it, please check out our sponsors in the description. And now, here's my conversation

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: with Michael Mina. We spoke a year ago about rapid at-home testing, and I think you think

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: it should have been, still should be a big part of the solution to COVID. So let's recap. Where do

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: things stand today in terms of rapid at-home testing? Well, it's certainly something that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: you're right, I do think we should have them today. We've now had almost 20 months of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: living in anxiety, uncertainty, being afraid for our health, for our family's health, for our friends,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: shutdowns, economic instability. Everything has been uncertain because of this virus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: And then there's this little test. And it's the first time for many people that they're using it

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: and they're feeling empowered. They're feeling like they can control their little slice

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: of this pandemic. So as these tests have come out and more and more Americans have had an

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: opportunity to go and buy them from CVS or Walgreens or wherever they're at,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: I think that it's really shifting the tenor of the discussion. For a long time, all of 2020,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: it was like, I often felt like it was me and a few other people against the world. These tests

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: should be public health tools. These tests are infectiousness indicators. They shouldn't be

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: compared to PCR. All of these different things. And we could, of course, go through and recap

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: what the benefits and the metrics are that we should be looking at. But the point is, last year

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: and most of this year was about educating scientists, educating public health leaders,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: educating physicians to get them to understand that there is a different reason to test in a

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: pandemic than purely diagnostics and transmission blockade and severing transmission chains is the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: big one. So now I think we're at a point where people are now understanding. And they're

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: understanding because they are feeling it. They're holding it and they're doing it and they're

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: feeling the delight of seeing a negative and saying, I feel more comfortable. It's not perfect,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: but it's pretty darn close to perfect to allowing me to go and see my mom without mistakenly

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: infecting her or whatever the story might be. And now that that's happening, I think all of a sudden

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: we're seeing a massive change politically for these tests. Biden just came out the COVID-19

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: action plan the other day and one of the main pillars of it was testing and in particular

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: bringing rapid tests, scaling them up. So on that front, I think finally there is success. People

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: are actually understanding and I haven't stopped beating this drum for far too long and I like hate

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: rapid tests now. So maybe it's good to step back. Would you say most Americans have not taken a

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: rapid at home test? Absolutely. Most have definitely not taken a rapid test. So like

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: many of them probably don't know. They kind of probably say testing, they have like memories

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: of testing, like PCR testing that they have to go into somewhere and they have to like a swab deep

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: in their nose and that's the experience. Or maybe if you have to travel like Canada or something

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: like that, you have to get tested, that kind of stuff. So what are rapid at home tests?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: Yeah. So the rapid at home tests are, I like to call them paper strip tests. They're simple tests

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: that I wish I brought some today, but I didn't. They're simple tests that you swab at the moment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: most of them use a swab that you just swab the front of your nose. So it's not one of the deep

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: swabs that goes into your brain. And so it's not very uncomfortable. It's just like picking your

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: nose if you'll, and you put that swab into a little tube and the tube has some liquid in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: And then you put a few drops of that liquid onto a paper strip or you drop the paper strip into the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: tube, just like one of those indicators for the pool. And if you just like a pregnancy test,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: then if you get two lines, you're positive, one line, you're negative. It's super simple. It takes

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: 30 seconds once you know how to do it of hands-on time and you wait around 10 minutes and then you

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: read the result. They are extraordinarily effective to answer one question, am I infectious?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: And that is the public health question that we need to answer and consistently ask during this

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: pandemic, are you infectious? Am I infectious? Because it's only when we know that we're infectious

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: that we can be empowered to not mistakenly infect others. The PCR test is a little different

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: and we can go into the pros and cons, but one of the major differences is that a PCR test

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: gets a lot of people talking about the PCR test say it's much more sensitive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: And at an analytical level, it is. It can detect one molecule instead of 100,000. But for public

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: health, we don't want a test that can detect one molecule. In fact, that has created a net negative

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: for public health. We just want to know, am I infectious? And to know that question, to know if

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: I'm infectious, I only need a test that is going to be positive if I have a high viral load.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: Like a million. And when the virus grows so fast, it will grow from zero to a billion in a day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: So you don't really need, even on the front end of an infection, you don't need better sensitivity

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: if the trade-off is that you don't get the result for one, two, or three days. You absolutely want

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: a rapid result that can tell you, yes, you're infectious. You're transmitting to others right

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: now. And I'm going to give you the result right now. So it is a much more effective tool because

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: it's fast, because it's accessible. We can use them in the home. And there's some issues with

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: using them at home. We can talk a little bit about what those issues are, like reporting and how do

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: you use everything on the honor system if you have a test that you're taking at home and you use it

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: to go to work. But they can be accessible. PCR has to go into a lab. It takes a lot of time for some

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: to get a PCR test. They either have to go online and order it. It takes the next day for it to come

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: back. They swab themselves. They ship it out the next day. And then they get a result two days later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: That's four days minimum for the most part. And at that point, you're not even infectious,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: even if you did happen to be infectious when you first ordered the test. So it's really the speed

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: of these tests and the accessibility and distribution of them that makes them so immensely powerful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: So you have this amazing graphic you tweeted. It's exactly what you're saying, which is a rapid

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: antigen test answers the question, am I currently infectious? And you have, I think, a comparison of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: seven different tests based on the viral load. And based on the viral load across these different

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: tests, you look at the likelihood of infectiousness. So what does this graphic show? We can overlay

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: that for people. I think it's just really nice and really clear. Yeah. So what that's showing is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: we can never ask what's the sensitivity of a test and just let that be the answer. That's what the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: FDA does currently. And that question doesn't mean anything. We have to say, what is the sensitivity

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: of the test to detect what? And so we can have different viral loads. For example, you can have

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: a viral load of one or you can have a viral load of a trillion. And a PCR test will tell you that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: you are positive, regardless of whether it's one or a trillion. So we can't ask the question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: how sensitive is a rapid test compared to PCR, because that covers the whole gamut. What we

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: really want to say is, how sensitive is the rapid test to detect me if I am infectious?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: And that gets to about 97% or so sensitive. If the question is, how likely is it to detect me

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: if I'm a super spreader? That's a really important one to be able to detect. They're all about 100%

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: sensitive. So if you have extraordinarily high viral loads to the point where you might be a

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: super spreader, these simple rapid tests will essentially always catch you until you're positive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: And then as you go down the line, if you're no longer infectious at all, then these rapid tests

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: might have a 0% sensitivity compared to PCR, but that's actually a good thing. The FDA and others

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: look at it as though it's a bad thing because they average it all together and say, oh, this is only

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: a 40% sensitive test compared to PCR. But that's not the right way to look at it. You want to say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: well, out of all of those samples, how many of them were not transmissible? How many were mid,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: moderate, high, extremely high, super spreader? And you should at the very least create a weighted

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: one of them is positive, then you basically say, we have to retest everybody in the pool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: Or like- Yeah. So you take, let's say you have a school and each classroom, you might have 20 kids,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: each swab their nose in a classroom, and all those swabs go into a single tube. And then you rinse

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: that tube out with some saline and you run a PCR test on that tube of 25 samples, 20 samples.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: And so if that tube turns positive in the PCR test, then all 20 or 25 of those students

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: are now having to quarantine. And if there's no positive, then all 20 or 25 students are

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: interpreting that their result is negative. So it really is ridiculous decision by the FDA to say

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: that if the test itself only tests one sample at a time, it's medicine, because it will tell you one

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: person at a time if you're positive or if you're negative. But if you do it as a pool and you tell

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: 25 people that your pool was negative, then that's somehow different. That's public health, not

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: medicine. It doesn't make, there's no logic there. Was it just personalities and accidents of history

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: or something like that? For example, you talk about the public health tools and CDC, you look at masks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: So masks were decided to somehow be an effective tool to help with the pandemic. So I'm sure

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: tests. I was very much reading a lot of research on masks. It's tricky. It's really tricky to show

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: how well they stopped the transmission of a virus, especially when you don't fully understand how the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: virus is transmitted or the viral load required, all that kind of stuff. But then the CDC pretty

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: quickly decided masks or whatever, there's some oscillations back and forth, but then they quickly

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: decided, everybody decided masks is a good tool. So masks being decided a good tool and then

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: rapid antigen tests, not a good tool. Is that just like certain personalities who didn't speak up

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: in a meeting or who did speak up in a meeting? Is this just like a weird roll of the dice or is there

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: a better explanation? I think it's somewhat of a roll of the dice, but I also think it's that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: testing. So doctors don't pretend to really understand much about fluid dynamics and

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: how well masks are working. That's way out of their realm. Doctors do believe that they understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: all aspects of the tests. And so the greatest barriers to rapid tests being brought to market

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: or being rolled out heavily and supported as public health tools, the greatest barriers came

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: from physicians saying, hell no, we can't use a test that's not as sensitive as a PCR.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: And look at what happens if you use this antigen test and not a PCR test, you get people who are

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: showing a positive on a PCR and negative on an antigen. And they just assume that that was

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: a false negative on the antigen. For public health, I would call it a false positive on the PCR test.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: But this type of thinking literally does not exist in medicine. And I think the biggest problem here

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: is that we placed physicians in decision-making power. When this pandemic hit, everyone called up

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: clinical laboratory folks and microbiologists and physicians to ask, well, what kind of test should

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: we use, that kind of thing. And there is no training in medical school for this kind of public

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: health work. You have to optimize on the right qualities of a test that have nothing to do with

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: medicine. And then sometimes, if not frequently, they're actually at odds. And I'll give an example

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: why the physicians, you could see why the physicians would have been against it from their

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: perspective. And they say, if a physician is a TSA agent at the airport, a TSA agent, their role

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: at any given time and the role they think that the instruments need to play is, I want you to scan

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: the bag as well as possible. This is the only bag that I'm interested in at the moment. And this is

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: my lane. This is my bag. I want to make sure that my instrument's doing. I don't want the crappy

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: instrument in my lane. I want to make sure that I'm doing everything I can. But what those TSA

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: agents don't have to worry about is, well, how many other instruments are there in this airport? Is

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: anyone getting through the lines here without going through security? The average TSA agent doesn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: have to worry about that. They literally have one job to do, and it's pay attention to this lane.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: If there's a big gap in the security line and people are flowing through without going through

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: security, that's not on the TSA agent. That's not a big systematic problem of the system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: And we can't expect that TSA agent to have ever even thought about that. That's not on them. They

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: were trained to look at the bag. And that's like physicians. And they're like, well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: that's kind of like physicians. And probably some physicians will hear this and feel like

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: I'm insulting. I don't mean to be likening the two professions or anything like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: The point is that a physician has one duty. Do no harm to this patient. Time is an of the essence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: Scale. How many tests can my hospital perform in a day? How many tests can my county or country

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: perform in a day? That's not a physician's training to think like that at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: And so what has happened is doctors got on board early and said, oh, hell no. We've seen these

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: antigen tests before. They're not particularly sensitive compared to PCR. And early in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: pandemic, there was like pissing matches between labs who had the most sensitive PCR. And it just

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: distracted everything. I was trying to say pretty early, like we don't need sensitivity. We

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: just need frequency. We just need scale. We need to think differently because our only goal, if

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: we're doing frequent routine testing of asymptomatic people, is not medicine. It's to say, do you need

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: to isolate now? And if you have a PCR test that's taking three days to return, and you're like... If

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: I was currently spreading virus before I walked in here and you handed me... This actually happened

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: something before your workday is done. And I'm looking at it. I'm like, what is this going to

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: do? What if I'm super spreader right now? You're giving me free rein to walk around and infect

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: everyone in the school, and you're going to give me my result to tell me I did that in two days

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: from now? It doesn't really make sense. So who is supposed to be... It's understandable that doctors

body.input: just any company start shipping them in the US because that would create pandemonium and we'd

body.input: like six to 12 months to run trials. They're failing because they can't keep up with PCR.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: through this and don't figure out how to evaluate a damn rapid test. So how do vaccines play with

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: once you have a vaccine, COVID is solved. So how does that interplay? Like, why do we still need

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: or something that was titled, Why We Still Need Rapid Tests With Vaccines. And the real reason

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: is because we have evaluated our vaccines based on their ability to stop disease. In fact, most of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: evaluate that at all, no less put it as one of the metrics for authorization. And with a virus like

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: this, it would be a bit naive to think that it's really going to stop transmission well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: I think a lot of excitement happened right after the first clinical trials, and I'm sure we were

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: talking about it when I was last here, I would imagine, given the timing. But those first

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: clinical trials came out and everyone jumped for joy that these things were going to be the end to

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: this pandemic. But we had really short-sighted vision there by not recognizing two main features.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: One is that they might not stop transmission. Another, I guess three, another is that new

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: variants might come around that will break through the vaccine protective immunity. And the third is

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: that we were measuring the efficacy of these vaccines during the peak of their performance

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: in the first few months after people got vaccinated. And that gives a skewed view of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: just how effective these are going to be long-term. So what happened with the vaccines is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: everyone got very comfortable, including the CDC saying, if you've been vaccinated, this is the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: end of the pandemic for you and let's keep it up. But then Delta comes along and waning immunity

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: comes along and both of these things compound exactly as anticipated to get breakthrough cases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: And unfortunately, what we're seeing now is the CDC and the administration went so

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: all in on saying that breakthrough cases are rare, that transmission doesn't really happen

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: if you're vaccinated without great data, especially with Delta, that once you get

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: that once people started seeing breakthrough cases, they started interpreting that as a

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: failure of the vaccine. The vaccines are still working to keep people out of the hospital

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: for the most part, but they're not working to stop transmission. And if our goal is to stop

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: transmission, which until we decide as a society that we have different goals, like we're okay

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: with people getting ill and letting transmission go because we don't want to worry about it anymore,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: we're not there yet. So until we decide that we're not going to stop transmission, we need

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: other avenues besides the vaccine because it's not doing it. It also means that herd immunity

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: isn't going to happen. And unfortunately, as long as we keep letting spread happen in the context of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: vaccinated people, we're kind of giving this virus a boot camp of exactly what it needs to

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: do and mutate to get around our vaccine-derived antibodies. And that makes me very nervous. So

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: the more we can do to stop spread in the unvaccinated, in the elderly vaccinated,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: and in other people, the better. We just should be focusing on that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: So in your eyes, the solution would look like this. You would make enough tests where every

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: testing program. It doesn't have to be complicated. Every household has a box of tests in their

body.input: cupboard. And if you haven't seen any cases in your community for a long time, stop testing. Do

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: That's a nice way to paint a map of the intensity of the virus. Okay, so when it goes above a certain

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: level, you can start doing much higher frequency testing in each household. That's right. So I

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: don't want people to be in testing purgatory. That's not what I want. I just want us to get

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: through this damn pandemic. And so we can monitor the wastewater or any other methods. We can

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: monitor the hospitals and the clinics. And if somebody does come in with COVID-like symptoms

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: and then a few other people come in, you realize, okay, we got spread happening in our community.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: Send out a text message, put it on the news, put in the newspaper, whatever you need to do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: tell people, tell families, use your test. And if the cases get worse, because you're just doing it

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: once a week, that's not going to stop transmission, but it's going to enable you to identify where

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: outbreaks are happening. If you start to find outbreaks in pockets, then the rule is simply,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: okay, let's squash the outbreak real fast. So everyone in that area, uncertain zip code or

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: whatever it might be, test every two days for seven days or every day for seven days,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: and you'll get rid of the outbreak. We can do that. And if you've now gone again a week or two with

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: no cases identified, stop the testing again. That's the nice thing that everything changes

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: when people have the tests in their home. It becomes dynamic. It can become easy. Send a

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: text message, take your test today. If some people don't do it, that's fine. The only goal

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: is to get R below one and you stop the outbreak. People think it has to be near perfect. I always

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: hear people say, what if somebody doesn't use it? Or what if somebody lies? Well, you have 98% of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: people testing or even 50%, that's a whole lot better. And another big difference that people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: I think oftentimes have a problem wrapping their head around, especially to an extent

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: physicians who are used to different kinds of metrics is that all we have to do to completely

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: stop an outbreak from spreading in a community is to get for every 100 infected people, to get them

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: to go on and infect 95. Most people would say, oh my God, that's a horrible, that's a horrible

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: program. You're still letting 100 people go and infect 95 people. But for a virus like this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: that's a massive public health win. If you can get 100 people to infect 90, most people, doctors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: I would say, like a lot of people would say that sounds like a failure, to be honest. But if you

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: do that for multiple days in a row, then in a couple of weeks, you've gone from a big outbreak

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: to a very, very small outbreak. And on the other hand, if you don't do that, if you don't do that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: if you allow 100 people to just infect 140 people, because you're not doing the testing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: then instead of having 20 people at the end of those four weeks with the testing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: you literally would have 600. It's massive differences here. And the only goal then is

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: to get R below one, have 100 people infect less than 100, and you stop the outbreaks and

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: everyone stays safe. From everything you've seen, how cheap can these things get? From like in the

body.input: past year, in terms of the developments you've seen with the various test manufacturers, how

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: cheap can it be to make a test, to manufacture a test?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: So there's the manufacturing process, that could be 50 cents, maybe less. It's hard to get,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: much it costs per test. You look at a place with high market competition that has actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: that's, and they're still making a profit. And so it's extremely cheap, market competition can

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: drive these tests way down in terms of cost. I think one of the most important features

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: these, the primary mode should be just get people tests, but really, if you're going to be using it

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: to make sure that their people are testing. So are you going to base it on the honor system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: I would say you probably would not base testing on the honor system if it's like to

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: take somebody who would otherwise be quarantined in school and say you can go to school as long

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: but they don't want to set up nursing stations in their lobbies or in the school parking lot or

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: whatever. Everyone's tired of that. We need to bring the test into the home, but that means

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: we need the technology to enable it. So I was at a conference recently, do you know Mike Milken?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: Milken Institute, he's a very wealthy billionaire, but he's done a lot of philanthropy and he hosts

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: Francis Collins and a number of other people were there. Every morning we all had to test,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: which I thought was a great idea obviously before we walked into that conference, but you didn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: have to test there and they didn't base it on the honor system. Every morning I scanned a QR code on

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: on my phone or on my computer and said, okay, let's go through your test. And I was like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: and said, okay, let's go through your tests. And they watch you, they videotape you using the test,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: so it's all recorded, it's all a reportable type of test. And at the end of it, just from your home,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: you don't actually see the proctor, but they're just verifying that you actually do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: They verify the test, they verify the test results with you. And at the end of it, you've then gotten

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: from your couch or from your car, wherever you are, an actual verified laboratory report

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: that can be considered proof that you yourself used the test and you yourself got a negative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: So the tools are out here if we want to use them at scale. And in fact, the CDC uses eMed now to

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: enable people to come back into the United States through an antigen test. So before you get on your

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: use your eMed test and you get the negative and CDC will accept that. TSA will accept you to come

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: back into the U.S. with a rapid antigen test that you did without anyone else watching,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: except for this proctor on your phone. Super simple.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: How much private information is being collected? So like this, you know, people have in the United

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: States, the American way, they have a hesitancy on the overreach of government in things like

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: see there a way of achieving testing that's verified but does not violate people's privacy

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: or sense of freedom? Absolutely. I think so. The way that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: right now in the United States, they're requesting that these tests get, that the results get

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: delivered to public health agencies. But I've long held that while that's ideal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: it should never be the thing that holds up somebody being allowed to know their own status.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: But if you are going to work and you have to let your boss or your manager,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: name. But sure, I mean, could you cut off the public health reporting? Yes, you could. But I

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: out of the public health reporting because for whatever reason, otherwise I'm not going to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: the test. But that means that, okay, then you're not going to go to school.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: and I am very uncomfortable with the idea that we force anyone to do anything, but there is a

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: tension between these two things for sure. And how do you balance that during a public health

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: emergency? I think first and foremost, let people, everyone has a right to know their status.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: The fact that we have made it hard for people to know their status on their terms, I think is a

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: travesty. I mean, it's just so terrible that we have prioritized us knowing at the expense of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: you know, essentially what public health has long said during this pandemic is if I'm public health,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: if I can't know, then you can't know your status. Like that's not the right way to look at public

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: health. We need to engage the public. And if some of them don't want to participate in the public

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: health part, but want to know their status, by default they are participating in public health,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: whether they know it or not, because they're not going to go get their mom sick by mistake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: that you're negative, but that doesn't require reporting it. You can, like there might be

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: basically like an ID that's only in possession. You are the only person in possession of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: agencies. But let's say there was something a little different. Let's say you were verifying

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: an over-the-counter test and it doesn't have to be a CLIA waived because it's over the counter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: Then you're not bound by CLIA rules and you could create the same service, but that just doesn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: the only way that they will use it is if it's not reported, then that's better than no test.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: distrust of government. So you're asking people to get tested and report their status

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: sense. It seems like a perfect solution to let people who are hesitant on a vaccine

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: to get their own status and have full control of that information and opt in, provide that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: information if they wish to, but they have the full control of it and have the freedom to do that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: services and we could have the privacy if you want it. If you need to go into a restaurant and

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: who want to be the public health agents of this pandemic. We lose a lot of control because the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: companies ultimately have to do what's going to make them money so they survive and keep performing

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: I was probably really pushing for the government to be producing these tests. I think I would have

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: still been pushing for that. At this point, I've decided, okay, the government's clearly not going

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

body.input: serious that these tests are simple to make, but we've been using machines to make them that have

body.input: been around for a long time. Scale is an issue right now, kind of. Really, it's the EUA process

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Mina: Rapid COVID Testing | Lex Fridman Podcast #235

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: It was somewhere between a long relationship and Stockholm syndrome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: When I first started my PhD, I knew I wanted to learn about molecular spectra and how to

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: simulate it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: I thought it was really outraged, outrageous that we as a species couldn't detect molecules

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: remotely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: We didn't have this perfect catalog ready of the molecular fingerprint of every molecule

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: we may want to find in the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And something as basic as phosphine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: The fact that we didn't really know how it interacted with light.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And so we couldn't detect it properly, you know, in the galaxy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Just I was so indignant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And so initially I just started working on phosphine because people hadn't before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And I thought we should know what phosphine looks like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And that was it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And then I read every paper that's ever been published about phosphine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: It was quite easy because there aren't that many.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And that's when I started learning about where we had already found it in the universe and

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: what it meant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: I started finding out quite how little we know about it and why.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And it was only when I joined MIT and I started talking to biochemists that it became clear

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: that phosphine wasn't just weird and special and understudied and disgusting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: It was all these things for oxygen loving life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And it was the anaerobic world that would welcome phosphine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And that's when the idea of looking for it on other planets became crystallized because

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: oxygen is very powerful and very important on earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: But that's not necessarily going to be the case on other exoplanets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Most planets are oxygen poor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Overwhelmingly most planets are oxygen poor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And so finding the sign of life that would be welcomed by everything that would live

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: without oxygen on earth seemed so cool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: But ultimately the project that first was born out of the idea that you want to find

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: that molecular fingerprint of a molecule.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And this is just one example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And that's connected to then looking for that fingerprint elsewhere in a remote way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And obviously at that time where exoplanets already, when you were doing your PhD, and

body.input: by the way, I should say your PhD thesis was on...

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Got it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195
