metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: But at that time when you're writing it, there's already a sense that exoplanets are out there

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: and we might be able to be looking for biosignatures on those exoplanets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Pretty much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: So I finished my PhD in 2015.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: We found the first exoplanets in the mid to late 90s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: So exoplanets were known.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: It was known that some had atmospheres.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And from there, it's not a big jump to think, well, if some have atmospheres, some of those

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: might be habitable and some of those may be inhabited.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: So how do you detect, you started to talk about it, but can we linger on it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: How do you detect phosphine on a far away thing, rocky thing, rocky planet?

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: What is spectroscopy?

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: What is this molecular fingerprint?

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: What does it look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: You've kind of mentioned a wave, but what are we supposed to think about?

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: What are the tools?

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: What are the uncertainties?

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: All those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: So the path can go this way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: You've got light, kind of pure light.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: You can crack that light open with a prism or a spectroscope or water and make a rainbow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: That rainbow is all the colors and all the invisible colors, the ultraviolet, the infrared.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And if that light was truly pure, you could consider that rainbow to just cover continuously

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: all of these colors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: But if that light goes through a gas, we may not see that gas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: We certainly cannot see the molecules within that gas, but those molecules will still absorb

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: some of that light, some, but not all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Each molecule absorbs only very specific colors of that rainbow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And so if you know, for example, that shade of green can only be absorbed by methane,

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: then you can watch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: As a planet passes in front of a star, the planet's too far away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: You can't see it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And it has an atmosphere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: That atmosphere is far too small.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: You definitely can't see it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: But the sunlight will go through that atmosphere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And if that atmosphere is methane, then on the other side, that shade of blue, I can't

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: remember if I said blue or green, that color will be missing because methane took it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And so with phosphine, it's the same thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: It has specific colors, 16.8 million colors, that it absorbs it and nothing else does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And so if you can find them and notice them missing from the light of a star that went

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: through a planet's atmosphere, then you'll know that atmosphere contains the molecule.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: How cool is that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: That's incredible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: So you can have this fingerprint within the space of colors and there's a lot of molecules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And I mean, I wonder, that's a question of like how much overlap there is, how close

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: can you get to the actual fingerprint?

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Like can phosphine unlock the iPhone with its lights on?

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: He said 16.8 billion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: So presumably this rainbow is discretized into little segments somehow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: How many total are there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: How a lot is 16.8 billion?

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: It's a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: We don't have the instruments to break these, break any light into this many tiny segments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And so with the instruments we do have, there's huge amounts of overlap.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Methane, as an example, a lot of the ways it's detectable is because the carbon and

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: the hydrogens, they vibrate with one another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: They move, they interact, but every other hydrocarbon, acetylene, isoprene has carbon

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: and hydrogens also vibrating and rotating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And so it's actually very hard to tell them apart at low resolutions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And our instruments can't really cope with distinguishing between molecules particularly

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: But in an ideal world, if we had infinite resolution, then yes, every molecule's spectral

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: features will be unique.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Yeah, like almost too, like it would be too trivial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: At the quantum level, they're unique.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: At our level, there's huge overlap.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And hopefully they're missing in a certain kind of pattern where you can say with some

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: kind of probability that it's this gas, not this gas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: So you're solving that gaseous puzzle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: I got it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: We can go back to Venus actually and show that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: So I study the quantum behavior of molecules, hence the quantum and the chemist specifically

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: so I can detect them in space, hence the astro.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: So what I do is I figure out the probability of a molecule being in a particular state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: There's no deterministic nature to the work I do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: But if you get a population of that molecule, it will always happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And so this is all at the quantum level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: I don't remember it by heart.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And what this means is I'm solving these giant quantum matrices.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And that's why you need a lot of computer power, giant computers to diagonalize these

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: enormous matrices, each of whom describes a single vibrational behavior of a molecule.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: So I think phosphine has 17.5 million possible states it can exist in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And transitions can occur between pairs of these states.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And there's a certain likelihood that they'll happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: This is the quantum world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Everything is deterministic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: There's just a likelihood that it will jump from one state to another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And these jumps, they're transitions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And I think in science, there's this really destructive notion of the lone wolf, the scientist

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: who sees things where others don't, then that's really appealing and people really like either

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: fulfilling that or pretending to be fulfilling that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And first of all, it's mostly a lie.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Any modern scientist, particularly in astronomy, which is so interdisciplinary, any modern

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: scientist that's doing it on their own is doing a crappy job, most likely, because you

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: need an independent set of eyes to help you do things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: You need experts in the subfields that you're working on to check your work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: But most importantly, it's just a bad idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: It doesn't lead to good science and it leaves you miserable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: I was recently, I had some work that I was avoiding and I thought, maybe I should pursue

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: be a lot of hard work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And I was trying to balance these two things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: It can be really difficult and the outcome is that maybe 10 people will cite me in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: next decade because it's not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: No one's asking for this question to be answered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And then I found myself working with this collaborator, Jason Dipman, and I spent a

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: whole afternoon, hours with him working on this and time flew by.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And I just felt taller and like I could breathe better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: I was happier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: I was a better person when it was done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And that's because he's a great collaborator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: He's just a wonderful person that brings out joy out of science that you're doing with

body.input: him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: stop worrying about being the lone wolf.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: It's just a terrible dream that will leave you miserable and your science will be shit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: And since I'm Russian, just murder anybody who doesn't fall into that beautiful collaborative

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: relationship.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: We were talking about books.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: Books, yes.

body.input: Is there books, movies?

body.input: But there's plenty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: I read about Danny Kahneman's work instead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: But when I was little, it was Contact, the Carl Sagan book, I really thought I was just

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

body.input: I find enormous relief in the absence of meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Clara Sousa-Silva: Searching for Signs of Life on Venus and Other Planets | Lex Fridman Podcast #195

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: What I was interested in is, how does something that we would usually identify as complexity

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: Look, I think that a very interesting question is, which I've certainly thought a little bit about,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: is what can you imagine? What is the sort of factoring of something, what are some other

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: possible ways you could exist, so to speak? Right. And if you were a photon, if you were

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: some kind of thing that was intelligence represented in terms of photons, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: the photons we receive in the cosmic microwave background, those photons, as far as they're

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: concerned, the universe just started. They were emitted 100,000 years after the beginning of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: universe. They've been traveling at the speed of light. Time stayed still for them. And then they

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: just arrived and we just detected them. So for them, the universe just started. And that's a

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: different perception of, that has implications for a very different perception of time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: They don't have that single thread that seems to be really important for being able to tell a heck

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: of a good story. So we humans- Yes. We can tell a story. Right. We can tell a story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: What other kind of stories can you tell? So a photon is a really boring story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: Yeah. I mean, so that's a, I don't know if they're a boring story, but I think it's,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: you know, I've been wondering about this and I've been asking, you know, friends of mine who are

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: science fiction writers and things, have you written stuff about this? And I've got one example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: great collection of books from my friend, Rudy Rooker, which I have to say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: they're books that are very informed by a bunch of science that I've done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: And the thing that I really loved about them is, you know, in the first chapter of the book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: the earth is consumed by these things he called NANTS, which are nano bot type things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: Nice. So, you know, so the earth is gone in the first, but then it comes back. But then-

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: Spoiler alert.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: Yeah, right. That was only a micro spoiler. It's only chapter one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: Okay. Good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: It's, but the thing that is not a real spoiler alert because it's such a complicated concept,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: but in the end, the earth is saved by this thing called the principle of computational equivalence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: which is a kind of a core scientific idea of mine. And I was just like, like thrilled. I don't read

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: fiction books very often. And I was just thrilled. I get to the end of this and it's like, oh my gosh,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: you know, everything is saved by this sort of deep scientific principle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: Can you maybe elaborate how the principle of computational equivalence can save a planet?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: That would, that would be a terrible spoiler for me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: There would be a spoiler. Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: Yeah. But no, but let me say what the principle of computational equivalence is. So the question is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: you are, you have a system, you have some rule, you can think of its behavior as corresponding

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: to a computation. The question is how sophisticated is that computation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: The statement of the principle of computational equivalence is as soon as it's not obviously

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: simple, it will be as sophisticated as anything. And so that has the implication that, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: rule 30, you know, our brains, other things in physics, they're all ultimately equivalent

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: in the computations they can do. And that's what leads to this computational irreducibility idea,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: because the reason we don't get to jump ahead, you know, and out think rule 30 is because we're

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: just computationally equivalent to rule 30. So we're kind of just both just running computations

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: that are the same sort of raw, the same level of computation, so to speak. So that's kind of the,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: the idea there. And the question, I mean, it's like, the, you know, in the science fiction version

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: would be, okay, somebody says, we just need more servers, get us more servers, the way to get even

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: more servers is turn the whole planet into a bunch of micro servers. And that that's, that's where it

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: starts. And so the question of, you know, computational equivalence, principle of

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: computational equivalence is, well, actually, you don't need to build those custom servers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: Actually, you can, you can just use natural computation to compute things, so to speak,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: you can use nature to compute, you don't need to have done all that engineering. And it's kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: the, it's kind of feels a little disappointing that you say, we're going to build all these servers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: we're going to do all these things, we're going to make, you know, maybe we're going to have human

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: consciousness uploaded into, you know, some elaborate digital environment. And then you look

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: at that thing and you say, it's got electrons moving around, just like in a rock. And then you

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: say, well, what's the difference? And the principle of computational equivalence says, there isn't,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: at some level, a fundamental, you know, you can't say mathematically, there's a fundamental

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: difference between the rock that is the future of human consciousness and the rock that's just a rock.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: Now, what I've sort of realized with this kind of consciousness thing is, there is a, there is an

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: aspect of this that seems to be more special, that isn't, and for example, something I haven't

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: really teased apart properly is when it comes to something like the weather and the weather having

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: a mind of its own or whatever, or your average, you know, pulsar magnetosphere acting like a sort

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: of intelligent thing, how does that relate to, you know, how is that entity related to the kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: consciousness that we have and sort of what would the world look like, you know, to the weather,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: if we think about the weather as a mind, what will it perceive? What will its laws of physics be?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: I don't really know. Because it's very parallel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: It's very parallel among other things. And it's not obvious. I mean, this is a really kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: mind bending thing, because we've got to try and imagine where, you know, we've got to try and

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: imagine a parsing of the universe different from the one we have. And by the way, when we think

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: about extraterrestrial intelligence and so on, I think that's kind of the key thing is, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: we've always assumed, I've always assumed, okay, the extraterrestrials, at least they have the

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: same physics. We all live in the same universe. They've got the same physics. But actually,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: that's not really right, because the extraterrestrials could have a completely different

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: way of parsing the universe. So it's as if, you know, there could be for all we know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: right here in this room, you know, in the details of the motion of these gas molecules,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: there could be an amazing intelligence that we were like, but we have no way of we're not parsing

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: the universe in the same way, if only we could parse the universe in the right way, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: immediately this amazing thing that's going on. And this, you know, huge culture that's developed

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: and all that kind of thing would be obvious to us. But it's not because we have our particular way

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: of parsing the universe. Would that thing also have an agency? I don't know the right word to

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: use, but something like consciousness, but a different kind of consciousness?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: I think it's a question of just what you mean by the word, because I think that this notion of

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: consciousness and the, okay, so some people think of consciousness as sort of a key aspect of it is

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: that we feel that there's sort of a feeling that we exist in some way, that we have this

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: intrinsic feeling about ourselves. You know, I suspect that any of these things would also

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: have an intrinsic feeling about themselves. I've been sort of trying to think recently

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: about constructing an experiment about what if you were just a piece of a cellular automaton,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: let's say, you know, what would your feeling about yourself actually be? And, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: can we put ourselves in the shoes, in the cells of the cellular automaton, so to speak?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: Can we get ourselves close enough to that, that we could have a sense of what the world will be

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: like if you were operating in that way? And it's a little difficult because, you know, you have to

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: not only think about what are you perceiving, but also what's actually going on in your brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: And our brains do what they actually do. And they don't, it's, you know, I think there might be some

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: experiments that are possible with, you know, neural nets and so on, where you can have something

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: where you can at least see in detail what's happening inside the system. And I've been sort

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: of one of my projects to think about is, is there a way of kind of getting a sense kind of from

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: inside the system about what its view of the world is and how it, you know, can we make a bridge?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: See, the main issue is this, where, you know, it's a sort of philosophically difficult thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: because it's like we do what we do. We understand ourselves, at least to some extent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: We humans understand ourselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: That's correct. And, but yet, okay, so what are we trying to do, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: when we are trying to make a model of physics? What are we actually trying to do? Because, you

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: know, you say, well, can we work out what the universe does? Well, of course we can. We just

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: watch the universe. The universe does what it does. But what we're trying to do when we make

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: a model of physics is we're trying to get to the point where we can tell a story to ourselves that

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: we understand that is also a representation of what the universe does. So it's this kind of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: you know, can we make a bridge between what we humans can understand in our minds

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: and what the universe does? And in a sense, you know, a large part of my kind of life

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: efforts have been devoted to making computational language, which kind of is a bridge between

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: what is possible in the computational universe and what we humans can conceptualize and think

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: about. In a sense, what, you know, when I built Wolfram Language and our whole sort of computational

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: language story, it's all about how do you take sort of raw computation and this ocean of

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: computational possibility and how do we sort of represent pieces of it in a way that we humans

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: can understand and that map onto things that we care about doing. And in a sense, when you add

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: physics, you're adding this other piece where we can, you know, mediate it by computer. Can we get

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: physics to the point where we humans can understand something about what's happening in it? And when

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: we talk about an alien intelligence, it's kind of the same story. It's like, is there a way of

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: mapping what's happening there onto something that we humans can understand? And, you know, physics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: in some sense, is like our exhibit one of the story of alien intelligence. It's an alien

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: intelligence in some sense. And what we're doing in making a model of physics is mapping that onto

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: something that we understand. And I think, you know, a lot of these other things that I've

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: recently been kind of studying, whether it's molecular biology, other kinds of things, which

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: we can talk about a bit, those are other cases where we're in a sense trying to again make that

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: bridge between what we humans understand and sort of the natural language of that sort of alien

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: intelligence in some sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: When you're talking about, just to backtrack a little bit, about cellular automata, being able

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: to, what's it like to be a cellular automata in a way that's equivalent to what it's like to be a

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: like for that local pocket of computation, what are you able to say about the broader...

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: Something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: And that somehow then can give you a sense of how to step outside of that cellular automata.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: Right. But the tricky part is that that little subset, what it's doing is it has a view of

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: itself. And the question is, how do you get inside it? It's like when we, with humans,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: it's like we can't get inside each other's consciousness. That doesn't really even make

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: sense. It's like there is an experience that somebody is having, but you can perceive things

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: from the outside, but getting inside it, it doesn't quite make sense. And for me, these

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: has been really interesting in thinking through some of these things is when it comes to questions

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: than watching this entity. So if you can somehow connect more and more, connect this full conscious

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: that represent where the planets are and so on. It's like a structural idea of how the universe

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: introduced into physics. And then we have this kind of idea of you write down some equation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: what happens in the universe is the solving of that equation. Time enters, but it's usually just

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: a parameter. We just can, you know, sort of slide it back and forth and say, here's where it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: Okay. Then we come to this kind of computational idea that I kind of started really pushing in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: early 1980s as a result, you know, the things we were talking about before about complexity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: that was my motivation. But the bigger story was the story of kind of computational models of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: And the big difference there from the mathematical models is in mathematical models,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: there's an equation, you solve it, you kind of slide time to the place where you want it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: In computational models, you give the rule and then you just say, go run the rule. And time is

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: not something you get to slide. Time is something where it just, you run the rule, time goes in

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: steps. And that's how you work out how the system behaves. You don't, time is not just a parameter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: time is something that is about the running of these rules. And so there's this computational

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: irreducibility, you can't jump ahead in time, but there's still, important thing is there's still

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: one thread of time. It's still the case, you know, the cellular automaton state, then it has the next

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: state and the next state and so on. The thing that is kind of, we've sort of tipped off by

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: quantum mechanics in a sense, although it actually feeds back even into relativity and things like

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: that, that there are these multiple threads of time. And so in this multi-computation paradigm,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: the kind of idea is instead of there being this single thread of time, there are these kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: distributed asynchronous threads of time that are happening. And the thing that's sort of different

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: all these different possible, you know, there's all these different paths. And so the only way you

body.input: can know what happened is to have some kind of observer who is saying, here's how to parse

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234

body.input: And models that are based on that. And this is similar to what people think about in non-deterministic

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Wolfram: Complexity and the Fabric of Reality | Lex Fridman Podcast #234
