body.input: And now here's my conversation with Don Song.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: Do you think software systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: will always have security vulnerabilities?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: Let's start at the broad, almost philosophical level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: That's a very good question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: I mean, in general, right, it's very difficult to write

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: completely bug-free code that has no vulnerability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: And also especially given that the definition of vulnerability

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: is actually really broad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: It's any type of attacks, essentially, on the code

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: can, you know, that's, you can call that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: that caused by vulnerabilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: And the nature of attacks is always changing as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: Like new ones are coming up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: Right, so for example, in the past,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: we talked about memory safety type of vulnerabilities

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: where essential attackers can exploit the software

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: and take over control of how the code runs

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: and then can launch attacks that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: By accessing some aspect of the memory

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: and be able to then alter the state of the program.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: Exactly, so for example, in the example of a buffer overflow,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: then the attacker essentially actually causes

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: essentially unintended changes in the state of the program.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: And then, for example, can then take over control flow

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: of the program and let the program to execute codes

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: that actually the program didn't intend.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So the attack can be a remote attack.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So the attacker, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: can send in a malicious input to the program

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: that just causes the program to completely

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: then be compromised and then end up doing something

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: that's under the attacker's control and intention.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: But that's just one form of attacks

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: and there are other forms of attacks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: Like for example, there are these side channels

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: where attackers can try to learn from

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: even just observing the outputs

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: from the behaviors of the program,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: try to infer certain secrets of the program.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So essentially, the form of attacks

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: is very broad spectrum.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: And in general, from the security perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: we want to essentially provide as much guarantee

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: as possible about the program's security properties

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So for example, we talked about providing

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: provable guarantees of the program.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So for example, there are ways we can use program analysis

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: and formal verification techniques

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: to prove that a piece of code

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: has no memory safety vulnerabilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: What does that look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: What does that prove?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: Is that just a dream that's applicable

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: to small case examples

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: or is that possible to do for real world systems?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So actually, I mean, today, I actually call it

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: that we are entering the area of formally verified systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So in the community, we have been working

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: for the past decades in developing techniques and tools

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: to do this type of program verification.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: And we have dedicated teams that have dedicated

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: their years, sometimes even decades

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: of their work in this space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So as a result, we actually have a number

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: of formally verified systems ranging from microkernels

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: to compilers to file systems to certain crypto libraries

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So it's actually really wide ranging

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: and it's really exciting to see

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: that people are recognizing the importance

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: of having these formally verified systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: with verified security.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So that's great advancement that we see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: But on the other hand, I think we do need to take

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: all these in essentially with the caution as well

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: in the sense that just like I said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: the type of vulnerabilities is very varied.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: We can formally verify a software system

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: to have certain set of security properties,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: but they can still be vulnerable to other types of attacks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: And hence, it's that we continue to need

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: to make progress in the space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So just a quick to linger on the formal verification.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: Is that something you can do

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: by looking at the code alone

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: or is it something you have to run the code

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: to prove something so empirical verification?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: Can you look at the code, just the code?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So that's a very good question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So in general, for most program verification techniques,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: it's essentially try to verify the properties

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: of the program statically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: And there are reasons for that too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: We can run the code to see, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: using like in software testing with fuzzing techniques

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: and also in certain even model checking techniques,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: you can actually run the code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: But in general, that only allows you to essentially verify,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: analyze the behaviors of the program

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: under certain situations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So most of the program verification techniques

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: actually works statically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: What does statically mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: Without running the code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: Without running the code, yep.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So, but sort of to return to the big question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: if we can stand for a little bit longer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: do you think there will always be security vulnerabilities?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: That's such a huge worry for people

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: in the broad cybersecurity threat in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: It seems like the tension between nations, between groups,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: the wars of the future might be fought

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: in cybersecurity security that people worry about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: And so of course, the nervousness is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: is this something that we can get ahold of in the future

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: for our software systems?

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So there's a very funny quote saying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: security is job security.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: So, right, I think that essentially answers your question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: Right, so we strive to make progress

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: in building more secure systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: and also making it easier and easier

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: to build secure systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: But given the diversity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: the various nature of attacks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: and also the interesting thing about security is that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: unlike in most other fields,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: essentially you are trying to, how should I put it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Dawn Song: Adversarial Machine Learning and Computer Security | Lex Fridman Podcast #95

body.input: prove a statement true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Cal Newport: Deep Work, Focus, Productivity, Email, and Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #166

metadata.title: Podcast: Cal Newport: Deep Work, Focus, Productivity, Email, and Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #166

body.input: Oh yeah.

body.input: people. That's when you look back on it. And I think that's a major surprise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: It's a surprise because-

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: that teaches you something because it's very clear that if it could happen in Germany,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: animals without feeling much of anything, it can the same. And when you feel that, I think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: I think that doesn't bring out the most generous aspect of human nature. So that Nazi soldier,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: you know, he was a good man. I mean, you know, he was perfectly capable of killing a lot of people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: you step in the street. And when you step in the street, you actually look away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Look away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Yeah. Now, what does that, what that's saying is, I mean, you're trusting that the car

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: who hasn't slowed down yet will slow down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Yeah. And you're telling him, I'm committed. I mean, this is like in a game of chicken.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: So I'm committed and if I'm committed, I'm looking away. So there is, you just have to stop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: So the question is whether a machine that observes that needs to understand mortality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Here, I'm not sure that it's got to understand so much as it's got to anticipate. So, and here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: but you know, you're surprising me because here I would think that maybe you can anticipate

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: without understanding, because I think this is clearly what's happening in playing gore

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: and playing chess has a lot of anticipation and there is zero understanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: So I thought that you didn't need a model of the human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: And the model of the human mind to avoid hitting pedestrians, but you are suggesting that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: That you do. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: You do. And then it's, then it's a lot harder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: So this is, and I have a follow up question to see where your intuition lies is it seems that

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: almost every robot human collaboration system is a lot harder than people realize.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: So do you think it's possible for robots and humans to collaborate successfully?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: We talked a little bit about semi-autonomous vehicles like in the Tesla autopilot,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: but just in tasks in general.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: If you think we talked about current neural networks being kind of system one, do you think

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: those same systems can borrow humans for system two type tasks and collaborate successfully?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Well, I think that in any system where humans and the machine interact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: the human will be superfluous within a fairly short time. That is if the machine is advanced

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: enough so that it can really help the human, then it may not need the human for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Now it would be very interesting if there are problems that for some reason the machine

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: doesn't cannot solve, but that people could solve. Then you would have to build into the

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: machine an ability to recognize that it is in that kind of problematic situation

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: and to call the human. That cannot be easy without understanding that it must be very difficult

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: to program a recognition that you are in a problematic situation without understanding

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: the problem. That's very true. In order to understand the full scope of situations that

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: are problematic, you almost need to be smart enough to solve all those problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: It's not clear to me how much the machine will need the human. I think the example of

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: chess is very instructive. I mean, there was a time at which Kasparov was saying that human-machine

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: combinations will beat everybody. Even stockfish doesn't need people and AlphaZero certainly

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: doesn't need people. The question is, just like you said, how many problems are like chess and

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: how many problems are the ones that are not like chess? Well, every problem probably in the end is

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: like chess. The question is how long is that transition period? That's a question I would

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: ask you in terms of autonomous vehicle just driving is probably a lot more complicated than Go

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: to solve that. Yes, and that's surprising. Because it's open. No, I mean, that's not surprising to me

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: because there is a hierarchical aspect to this, which is recognizing a situation and then within

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: the situation bringing up the relevant knowledge. And for that hierarchical type of system to work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: you need a more complicated system than we currently have. A lot of people think because

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: as human beings, this is probably the cognitive biases, they think of driving as pretty simple

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: because they think of their own experience. This is actually a big problem for AI researchers or

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: people thinking about AI because they evaluate how hard a particular problem is based on very

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: limited knowledge, basically on how hard it is for them to do the task. And then they take for granted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Maybe you can speak to that because most people tell me driving is trivial and humans, in fact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: are terrible at driving is what people tell me. And I see humans and humans are actually incredible

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: at driving and driving is really terribly difficult. Yeah. So is that just another element of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: effects that you've described in your work on the psychology side?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: No, I mean, I haven't really, I would say that my research has contributed nothing to

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: understanding the ecology and to understanding the structure of situations

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: and the complexity of problems. So all we know is very clear that that goal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: it's endlessly complicated, but it's very constrained. So in the real world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: there are far fewer constraints and many more potential surprises. So that's obviously,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: because it's not always obvious to people, right? So when you think about...

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Well, I mean, people thought that reasoning was hard and perceiving was easy, but they quickly

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: learned that actually modeling vision was tremendously complicated and modeling,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: even proving theorems was relatively straightforward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: To push back on that a little bit on the quickly part, it took several decades to learn that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: and most people still haven't learned that. I mean, our intuition, of course, AI researchers have,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: but you drift a little bit outside the specific AI field, the intuition is still perceptible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Oh, yeah. No, I mean, that's true. I mean, the intuitions of the public haven't changed

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: radically, and they are, as you said, they're evaluating the complexity of problems by how

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: difficult it is for them to solve the problems. And that's got very little to do with the

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: complexities of solving them in AI. How do you think from the perspective of AI researcher,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: do we deal with the intuitions of the public? So in trying to think, arguably, the combination of

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: hype investment and the public intuition is what led to the AI winters. I'm sure that same can be

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: applied to tech or that the intuition of the public leads to media hype, leads to companies

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: investing in the tech, and then the tech doesn't make the company's money, and then there's a crash.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Is there a way to educate people, sort of to fight the, let's call it system one thinking?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: In general, no. I think that's the simple answer. And it's going to take a long time before the

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: understanding of what those systems can do becomes public knowledge. And then, and the

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: expectations, there are several aspects that are going to be very complicated. The fact that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: have a device that cannot explain itself is a major, major difficulty. And we're already seeing

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: that. I mean, this is really something that is happening. So it's happening in the judicial

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: system. So you have a system that are clearly better at predicting parole violations than

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: judges, but they can't explain their reasoning. And so people don't want to trust them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: We seem to in system one even use cues to make judgments about our environment. So this

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: explainability point, do you think humans can explain stuff?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: No, but I mean, there is a very interesting aspect of that. Humans think they can explain themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: So when you say something and I ask you, why do you believe that? Then reasons will occur to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: But actually my own belief is that in most cases, the reasons have very little to do with why you

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: believe what you believe. So that the reasons are a story that comes to your mind when you need to

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: explain yourself. But people traffic in those explanations. I mean, the human interaction

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: depends on those shared fictions and the stories that people tell themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: You just made me actually realize, and we'll talk about stories in a second,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: that not to be cynical about it, but perhaps there's a whole movement of

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: people trying to do explainable AI. And really we don't necessarily need to explain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: AI doesn't need to explain itself. It just needs to tell a convincing story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Yeah, absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: The story doesn't necessarily need to reflect the truth. It just needs to be convincing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: There's something to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: You can say exactly the same thing. You know, we're talking about the human

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: interaction. There's something to that. You can say exactly the same thing in a way that

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: sounds cynical or doesn't sound cynical. But the objective of having an explanation

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: is to tell a story that will be acceptable to people. And for it to be acceptable and

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: to be robustly acceptable, it has to have some elements of truth. But the objective

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: is for people to accept it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: It's quite brilliant actually. So on the stories that we tell, sorry to ask you the question that

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: most people know the answer to, but you talk about two selves in terms of how life has lived.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: The experienced self and remembering self. Can you describe the distinction between the two?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Well, sure. I mean, there is an aspect of life that occasionally, you know, most of the time

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: we just live and we have experiences and they're better and they're worse and it goes on over time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: And mostly we forget everything that happens or we forget most of what happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Then occasionally, when something ends or at different points, you evaluate the past and you

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: form a memory and the memory is schematic. It's not that you can roll a film of an interaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: You construct, in effect, the elements of a story about an episode. So there is the experience and

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: there is the story that is created about the experience. And that's what I call the remembering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: So I had the image of two selves. So there is a self that lives and there is a self that evaluates

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: life. Now the paradox and the deep paradox in that is that we have one system or one self that

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: does the living, but the other system, the remembering self, is all we get to keep. And basically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: decision making and everything that we do is governed by our memories, not by what actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: happened. It's governed by the story that we told ourselves or by the story that we're keeping.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: So that's the distinction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: I mean, there's a lot of brilliant ideas about the pursuit of happiness that come out of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: What are the properties of happiness which emerge from the remembering self?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: There are properties of how we construct stories that are really important. So I studied a few,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: but a couple are really very striking. And one is that in stories, time doesn't matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: There's a sequence of events or there are highlights and how long it took. They lived happily ever after

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: or three years later, something. Time really doesn't matter. In stories, events matter, but time

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: doesn't. That leads to a very interesting set of problems because time is all we got to live. I

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: mean, time is the currency of life, and yet time is not represented basically in evaluated memories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: So that creates a lot of paradoxes that I've thought about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Yeah, they're fascinating. But if you were to give advice on how one lives a happy life

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: based on such properties, what's the optimal?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: Well, I gave up. I abandoned happiness research because I couldn't solve that problem. I couldn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: see. And in the first place, it's very clear that if you do talk in terms of those two selves,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: then what makes the remembering self happy and what makes the experiencing self happy

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: are different things. I asked the question of suppose you're planning a vacation and you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: just told that at the end of the vacation, you'll get an amnesic drug so you remember nothing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: and they'll also destroy all your photos, so there'll be nothing. Would you still go to the

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: same vacation? And it turns out we go to vacations in large part to construct memories,

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: not to have experiences, but to construct memories. And it turns out that the vacation

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: that you would want for yourself if you knew you will not remember is probably not the same

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: vacation that you will want for yourself if you will remember. So I have no solution to

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: these problems, but clearly those are big issues. And you've talked about how many minutes or hours

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: you spend about the vacation. It's an interesting way to think about it because that's how you

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: really experience the vacation outside the being in it. But there's also a modern, I don't know if

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: think I think I know what's going on? Actually, I mean, I have a theory about what's going on and

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: what's going on is that there is first of all, a very important discussion about the

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: subject is that there is first of all, a very important distinction between two types of

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: experiments. And one type is within subject. So the same person has two experimental conditions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: And the other type is between subjects, where some people have this condition, other people

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: have that condition. They're different worlds. And between subject experiments are much harder

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: to predict and much harder to anticipate. And the reason, and they're also more expensive

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: because you need more people and it's just, so between subject experiments is where the problem

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: is. It's not so much and within subject experiments, it's really between. And there is a very good

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: reason why the intuitions of researchers about between subject experiments are wrong. And that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: because when you are a researcher, you're in a within subject situation. That is you are imagining

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: the two conditions and you see the causality and you feel it. And, but in the between subject

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: condition, they don't, they see they live in one condition and the other one is just nowhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: So our intuitions are very weak about between subject experiments. And that I think is something

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: that people haven't realized. And, and in addition, because of that, we have no idea about the power

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: of manipulations of experimental manipulations, because the same manipulation is much more powerful

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: when, when you are in the two conditions than when you live in only one condition. And so

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: the experimenters have very poor intuitions about between subject experiments. And, and there is

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: something else, which is very important, I think, which is that almost all psychological hypotheses

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: are true. That is in the sense that, you know, directionally, if you have a hypothesis that a

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: really causes B that that it's not true that a causes the opposite B maybe a just has very

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: little effect, but hypotheses are true, mostly, except mostly they're very weak. They're much

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: weaker than you think when you are having images of. So the reason I'm excited about that is that I

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: recently heard about some, some friends of mine who they essentially funded 53 studies of behavioral

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: that people go to the gym. But, you know, and, and the success rate was zero. Not one of the 53 studies

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: work. Now what's interesting about that is those are the best people in the field, and they have no

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: idea what's going on. So they're not calibrated. They think that it's going to be powerful because

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: and it feels powerful to you. There's a thing that I've written about that's called the focusing

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: doesn't that mean you just report that? So what's, I guess, the solution to that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Daniel Kahneman: Thinking Fast and Slow, Deep Learning, and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #65

body.input: That's what I say to them every time I'm putting them to bed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Duncan Trussell: Comedy, Sentient Robots, Suffering, Love & Burning Man | Lex Fridman Podcast #312

body.input: Thank you, thank you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Duncan Trussell: Comedy, Sentient Robots, Suffering, Love & Burning Man | Lex Fridman Podcast #312

body.input: I'm Ozymandias.

metadata.title: Podcast: Duncan Trussell: Comedy, Sentient Robots, Suffering, Love & Burning Man | Lex Fridman Podcast #312

body.input: I met a traveler from an antique land who said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Duncan Trussell: Comedy, Sentient Robots, Suffering, Love & Burning Man | Lex Fridman Podcast #312

body.input: "'Two vast and trunkless legs of stone stand in the desert.

metadata.title: Podcast: Duncan Trussell: Comedy, Sentient Robots, Suffering, Love & Burning Man | Lex Fridman Podcast #312

body.input: Near them on the sand, half sunk, a shattered visage lies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Duncan Trussell: Comedy, Sentient Robots, Suffering, Love & Burning Man | Lex Fridman Podcast #312

body.input: whose frown and wrinkled lip and sneer of cold command

metadata.title: Podcast: Duncan Trussell: Comedy, Sentient Robots, Suffering, Love & Burning Man | Lex Fridman Podcast #312

body.input: tell that its sculptor, well those passions read,

metadata.title: Podcast: Duncan Trussell: Comedy, Sentient Robots, Suffering, Love & Burning Man | Lex Fridman Podcast #312

body.input: which yet survive stamped on these lifeless things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Duncan Trussell: Comedy, Sentient Robots, Suffering, Love & Burning Man | Lex Fridman Podcast #312

body.input: the hand that mocked them and the heart that fed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Duncan Trussell: Comedy, Sentient Robots, Suffering, Love & Burning Man | Lex Fridman Podcast #312

body.input: And on the pedestal, these words appear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Duncan Trussell: Comedy, Sentient Robots, Suffering, Love & Burning Man | Lex Fridman Podcast #312

body.input: Boundless and bare, the lone and level sands stretch far away."

metadata.title: Podcast: Duncan Trussell: Comedy, Sentient Robots, Suffering, Love & Burning Man | Lex Fridman Podcast #312

body.input: All gone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Duncan Trussell: Comedy, Sentient Robots, Suffering, Love & Burning Man | Lex Fridman Podcast #312

body.input: And despair.

metadata.title: Podcast: Duncan Trussell: Comedy, Sentient Robots, Suffering, Love & Burning Man | Lex Fridman Podcast #312

body.input: Even though we'll be forgotten in the sands of time,

body.input: Duncan, I'm just so glad that you exist
