metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And he's like, yo, you're one of those jerks who believes in creation. And I said, well, I do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: Well, what about the Big Bang Theory? He's going on this diatribe about the science and the gases

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: and the chemistry. And I'm going, dude, I barely got through high school chemistry, slow down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And he went on a tangent and all of a sudden I stopped and went,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: who created the gas and the molecules and the stuff you're talking about and the collisions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And he was furious and stomped off and I got him. And again, I had no facts, I had no figure,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: he didn't either, but I stumped him. But sometimes when you can't show something,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: people need to see something tangible. They need to see it in their hand to believe it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And that's the real hard thing about faith. I see it in action, people restore my faith.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And then I say to myself, well, there can't be that many dummies in this world if there's so

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: many billions of us believing in this higher power, this higher... And you said earlier,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: you believe most people are good and I do too. The bad outshine the good because the bad get the

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: press. If it bleeds, it leads. Think about it, how many more damn zombie apocalypse movies can we

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: make? I didn't even know there was that many zombies. And it just seems like every other show is

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: just guys bashing each other's heads in with bats with nails in it. And it's like after a while,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: it's like, oh gosh, you got to get a new boogeyman here. But seriously...

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: But meanwhile, human civilization is getting better and better. We just like making Hollywood

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: movies that just... We're getting better and better, but we're treating each other worse and

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: worse. You would think with all this technology and all the knowledge and all the... It's like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: what the hell is going on sometimes? I really want to see the good. And I think maybe the level of

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: bad that we're seeing was always existing. It's just now everything is instantaneous news and

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: flashes and tweets and this and this. Well, with the technology we have, it's also come to the

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: light. So you get to see all these fights. I think that's step one of dealing with the problem is

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: revealing it in its full, beautiful light. Oh yeah. How much of a bickering species we are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: 50 years ago, a guy like me who loves to talk, how the hell would I have gotten an opportunity

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: to have someone listen to me and have it, right? I love this. This is amazing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: I think it's cool. But you didn't have that arena. You didn't have all these things. My grandfather

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: Nels, God rest him, he died in 1979. That dude didn't even want to have a checking account.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: He would walk to each store, each, the phone company, the gas company, this company,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: and pay the bill in person. He didn't trust the bank. And it was like, now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: ATMs, this, that he would be overwhelmed. He'd be just like, I love my dad, but to watch him on his

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: iPad is comical, right? He calls my niece's boyfriend, who's a tech guy, Matt, if you listen,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: he's the greatest. He'll have this poor guy in a phone for hours. The second you're walking to

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: see my father, my kids, hey, do me a favor, straighten out this pad. And it's comical because

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: I'm looking at my dad and I'm going, he was born when Hitler started World War II.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And I'm going, he's seen all of that. Oh, my wife's grandmother was born in 1900 in Czechoslovakia

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: and she died in 1998. I'm going, holy, the stuff she saw in the span of her life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: it's just incredible. But what troubles me sometimes is with all of these advances and

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: all these devices, this is what I say to my kids, look up from the phone and look up, right? Because

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: we don't talk anymore. I saw a girl literally, I shouldn't say girl, guy, whatever, I saw a person

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: literally just about walking to an open manhole, called we're texting. And I'm going, that's scary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: That's scary because your awareness is gone. And I've been at restaurants,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: groups of people, and they're texting. They're texting each other, they're sitting on the other

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: side of the table. I'm like, put the freaking thing down and have a conversation. And that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: the thing, we've lost the art of conversation. My wife, she has this running joke, she goes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: there's a lot going on up there. And I'm like, yeah, because I really am inquisitive. I'm excited

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: about life. I love to meet people. I love to learn. And the only way you can do that is to

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: have a conversation. The hilarious thing about this, so you're obviously very charismatic. You

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: got great stories. You're a great human being. Thank you. You're talking to a guy who spent most

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: of his life behind a computer hiding from people. No, no. But we're trying to bridge this. Right,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: but I don't mean that as a rip, but I would never know that. It's real. I would never know that

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: because you're very engaging. I would not know. You don't have any impediments to your

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: social skills, your personal. And again, I don't mean it as a knock to you and these young people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: Well, no, but this is me trying to look up from a smartphone, is having these conversations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: talking to people. I think it's important. I mean, some of it could be, it's always hard to know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: Some of it could be just you and I being old school, because you grew up before the internet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: Maybe there is joy and deep human connection to be discovered inside the smartphone. It doesn't seem

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: that way. Yeah. Because the smartphone is so new, maybe we just haven't figured out those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: Because there's a globalizing aspect. There's an opportunity for you to connect with people from

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: across the world. Oh yeah. In ways that. I have cousins in Ireland and England. I love it. I get

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: a FaceTime or WhatsApp and it's like, holy crap, they're three, 4,000 miles away and I'm having a

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: conversation now. I used to send my grandma in Ireland a letter. I adored her. She passed when I

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: was 10. No, I'm sorry, I was 11. I sent her a letter, airmail and I'd wait and I'd wait.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And about two weeks later, this airmail letter would come back and she called me Master Nils

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: William Jorgensen. I would be so excited, open up that letter. Handwritten just like-

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: Yeah. And then I'd write her another one and I just couldn't wait for letters from granny.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And now it's like, that's kind of faded away. Yeah. I still write letters by the way, handwritten.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: I do too. The way this all came about was I wrote a letter to someone to say thank you for cancer

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: research. I'm blessed to be alive. That's a good starting point for any story. I'm blessed to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: alive. And my cancer was one that if I got it 15 years prior to 2000, I was a dead man.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: Right? 15, 20 years before there was no drug to treat. I was gone, going home to see him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: So there's this wonderful gentleman that donated hundreds of millions of dollars to cancer research,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: Mr. David Koch. He's since God rest his soul passed away. And he's a controversial guy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: big time business titan. And the press was just brutalizing him one day over something to do with

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: his politics. Now I'm a union guy, I'm proudly served in unions, still in a union. And he was

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: not, most business guys don't like unions, right? But most guys like me don't like working for $3

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: an hour. So we like our unions, right? And I reached out across the table, so to speak,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: and I sent him a handwritten letter to thank him, to say, we may not agree on everything,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: but I can't thank you enough. This is just this regular dude out there who is now living his life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: watching his kids grow. Thanks to generous people like you who believe enough in cancer research,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: you've saved my life. Maybe I can't say his exact dollars, but people like him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And he reached back out and his secretary said, oh, he'd like to talk to you on the phone. I go,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: well, he's kind of a busy guy. He wants to talk to me. He's a billionaire. And he got on the phone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: He was like the greatest guy in the world. Invited me up to Sloan Kettering to dedicate a new cancer

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: wing. It was like I was hanging out with my dad. And the sweetest man, just so kind,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: so empathy because he was a cancer survivor. But now he's got the means to help people who've

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: suffered his fate to a better place. And he was so real and it was so beautiful just to get to know

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: and say, hey, you know what? This guy is a big time guy, but yet he's just a regular human like

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: you and I. I'm a guy who went to night college and I went to the army and I'm a blue collar kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: dude. And here's this guy who went to MIT like you, and he's a wildly successful billionaire,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: a genius, but yet he can sit down and mix it up with me and know that I was truly grateful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And that to me was just like one of the coolest little relationships I've ever had. It wasn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: like we were hanging out, having barbecues together, but it was just, I was so touched by his decency.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: Well, the basics of the, like cancer reveals, it's like fundamental to the human experience

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: is trauma, is tragedy. It's like money, who gives a shit about money? Education, all that is like

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: weird new inventions. Life is short, you suffer with the various diseases, and that is a reminder

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: that life is short and a reminder of the basic human connection. And that's why you can bridge

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: that gap. All sparked by handwritten letter, which just makes for a hell of a story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And you know what, Lex? This is the commonality between us, a guy with three jobs to a billionaire.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: We both had that sense of a sledgehammer to the chest. Boom, you have cancer and you can't breathe

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: for like 30 seconds. And then when your heart's just about to kick off and you take a breath and

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: you go, I'm sorry, what'd you say, doc? You have cancer. And it don't matter what kind, one of my

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: best buddies, Bobby's going through right now, a prostate, and I got way too many of my buddies with

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: cancer, right? My buddy Hugh, who became a vet since his first cancer, he was a fireman, he's

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: now a veterinarian, right? He diagnosed me actually over the phone, by the way, when they couldn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: figure out what was wrong with me. Well, Dr. Hugh, he nailed it to the T. And we talk and the same

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: thing, the dozen of my close friends that have cancer, the same thing we say is the fear. So Mr.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: Coke and I, we shared that same sledgehammer to the chest and that same fear. And it didn't matter

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: how much money he had and how much I didn't. And you know, it's just like the morning of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: trade center. There was big time brokers who went to their demise, right? Working in these firms,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: God rest them. And there was dishwashers, excuse me, dishwashers up on the Windows on the World

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: restaurant on 107th floor making five bucks an hour and they died together. It didn't matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: It didn't matter if you had an armored car loaded with bills, you were done that day. And that's,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: I think where people need to humanize each other. Just because you drive around in a nice car and

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: you got your own jet and you got this and you got that, don't mean nothing. When you're going,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: when you're in that vulnerable spot, you could have more money than the US reserves, Federal Reserve,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: or you could have a welfare check. You're going. I learned that in a cancer ward. I had people in

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: my ward that died on me. I was going around as a little bit of an ambassador because I was trying

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: to, I was putting on a fake, I was putting on a fake like I got this, I got this. I was so scared.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: But when I got past that seven days of torture and the days leading up to it, I'd go around and try

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: to comfort the other cancer patients. I had just one older African American gentleman, he couldn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: talk because he had such advanced throat cancer. He was my roommate for a little while, but then

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: he got worse so they had to put him by himself. And you couldn't understand what he was saying

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: because his throat was just so radiated from the radiation. But if you put your ear

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: down to him, you could make out what he was saying. And I'm not faulting the nurses for maybe not

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: wanting to do that. They're busy. They got a ton going on. They can't spend. So if he was in need,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: I'd put my ear down and I'd find out and I'd go get it for him. So when they moved me down the hall,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: they asked me to come down with my IV tower. He needed me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And I knew it was bad because his look was gone. I said, sir, what do you need?

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And he whispered, call my sister, I'm going. He had only one survivor in his whole life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And she was in North Carolina and he wanted her to know she couldn't get up. She was elderly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And I got the nurse and I got on the phone and I called his sister and I said, ma'am,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: I explained who I was. And I said, he can't really verbalize too well right now, but he wants to

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: say he loves you. And I put the phone down and he told her he loved her and he said, I'm going home.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And that was it. And I hung the phone up and I said, ma'am, I'm so sorry. I said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: they'll notify you. And I stayed with him for a while holding his hand and then they wanted him

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: to rest. And then I left and then I got the tap an hour later and they said, I'm sorry he's gone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And then there was another girl and she was a young girl from one of the areas I worked,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: young African-American girl where I used to respond that I didn't know her, but I knew her

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: neighborhood and she had what I had, but they weren't sure which one, leukemias, there's an

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: elusive beast, there's 49 of them, right? And each one of them has got their own little nuances,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: own specific treatments. So if they don't know what you have, they don't know what to do for you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And she refused to let him drill into her hip to take the marrow because it's vicious,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: it hurts so much. It's like someone's boring into your hip with a wood drill and it's no joke.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And they asked me to try to convince her to let them do that or she was going to die

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: because if they couldn't figure it out, it was advancing quickly. So I talked to her and she

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: said, I can't, I'm too scared. I said, but are you more scared to die? And she said, I am. I said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: okay, I'll stay with you. I'll hold your hand. You squeeze it as hard as you want. I said, if you want,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: they'll give you like a towel or something to bite on, whatever. I said, but you get that pain

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: out, but you need to do this so you can get saved. And she said, okay. And they came in and they,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: this huge thick needle, they just bore it into you. And she's screaming for her life and she's

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: squeezing my fingers so hard and so hard. And I said, that's okay, hon, you keep going,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: you keep going. We got it. It's just 10 more seconds, 10 more seconds. They got it. They

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: figured out her treatment and they got her onto her road to recovery. And then I spent a long time

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: asking God, why do I have cancer? But then I stopped and I went, wait a minute,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: I didn't die that day with my friends. Shame on me for asking them why I have cancer. I had 10

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: years after 9-11 with such great years. And I got to watch my little girl being born when John never

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: got to see his son. So it was all gravy after that. And I said, but now I know why I have my cancer

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: because I can empathize with people who have it. And I can try to be their voice when they can't

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: talk, be their shield to try to take that pain because I can understand, I can walk their walk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: And now I thank God for my cancer because it's made me a better human being. It's made me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: I'm not going to lie, it brought a lot of anger for a while and my family suffered it, but I really

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: tried to go past that and heal and part of living out in the country. It's very, very healing for

metadata.title: Podcast: Niels Jorgensen: New York Firefighters and the Heroes of 9/11 | Lex Fridman Podcast #220

body.input: the mind and the soul. But I now thank God for the cancer because it humbled me. I didn't really need

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Well, you said the economy is a fascinating complex system, but it's made up of human

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: minds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And those are interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Those are interesting, perhaps impossible to model, but we can try and we can try to

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: figure out how to approximate them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And maybe that's the challenge of economics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So keep returning to the basics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Let us try to learn something from history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: I also see as part of economics is us trying to figure out stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And there's a few smart folks that write books throughout human history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And sometimes they name schools of economics after them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So let us take a stroll through history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Can you describe at a high level what are the different schools of economics, perhaps

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: ones that are interesting to you, perhaps ones that the difference between which reveals

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: something useful or insightful for our conversation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So you could, neoclassical, post-Kensian, Austrian, I like the biophysical economics

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: and so on, other heterodox economic schools that you find interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: I actually find interesting a school which went extinct about 250 years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: That's where I'd like to start from.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And they're called the Physicocrats.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And the name itself implies where their knowledge came from, because if you go back far enough

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: in history, we didn't do autopsies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: But when you started doing autopsies, they found wires, they found tubes, et cetera,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: They started seeing the body as a circulation system, and they applied the same sort of

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: logic to the economy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And they came out of an agricultural economy, which was France, and they saw that the wealth

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: came effectively from the sun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So they saw all wealth comes from, they said the soil, but what they really mean is the

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: soil absorbs the energy of the sun.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: One seed plants, a thousand flea seeds come back.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: There is no surplus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: We are simply mining what we can find out of the natural economy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: That's where we should have stayed and developed from that forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: We then went through the classical school of economics, which comes out of Adam Smith.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And Smith, coming from Scotland, looked at what the Physicocrats said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And what the Physicocrats argued was that agriculture is the source of all wealth, and

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: the manufacturing sector is sterile.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: That's literally the term they used to describe the manufacturing sector.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: What does sterile mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Sterile means you don't extract value.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: You simply change the shape of value.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So the value comes from the soil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Yeah, it comes from the soil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: That's the free gift of nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: That's literally the phrase they used.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And we then distribute the free gift of nature around, and we need carriages, which was the

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: manufacturing term they used at the time, as well as wheat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So to make the carriages, we take what's been taken from the soil, and we convert it to

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: a different form.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: But there is no value added in manufacturing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So Smith looked at that and said, well, I'm from Scotland.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And we've got these industries, you know, and we make stuff and it's machinery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And he said, no, it's not land that gives us the source of value, it's labor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Now that led to the classical school of thought, and that said that all value comes from labor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: That value is objective, so it's the amount of effort you put in, that the price two things

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: will exchange for reflects the relative effort that's involved in the manufacturing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So this computer takes two hours to make and this bottle takes two minutes to make, then

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: this is worth 60 times as much as that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: They didn't talk about marginal cost, it was absolute cost effectively.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: They didn't talk about utility as a subjective thing, they ridiculed subjective utility theory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: That led to Marx, and Marx is probably the most brilliant mind in the history of economics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: The only other competitor I'd see is Schumpeter, possibly Keynes, but in my terms of ranking

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: of intellects, so you have Marx, Schumpeter, Keynes in terms of the outstanding capacities

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: to think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: But Marx then turned that classical school, which was pro-capitalism and anti-feudal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: into a critique of capitalism, which led to the neoclassical school coming along as a

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: defense of capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: But they defended it using the ideas of the subjective theory of value, so that value

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: does not reflect effort, it's the satisfaction individuals get from different objects that

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: determines their value, marginal utility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: It's the marginal cost that determines how much they sell for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Capitalism equilibrates marginal cost and marginal utility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And the concepts of equilibrium and marginal this and marginal that became the neoclassical

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: school.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And that's still the dominant school now 150 years later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So that's the one that everybody learns, and when you first learn economics, if you don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: have the critical background that I managed to acquire, that's what you think is economics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: The marginal utility, equilibrium-oriented analysis of mainstream economics, and for

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: example, they ignore money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: People think economists, you must be an expert on money because you're an economist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Well, in fact, economists learn literally in the first few weeks at university that

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: money is irrelevant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: They say money illusion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: They represent people's tastes using what they call indifference curves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And they're like isoquants on a weather map.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: If you look at an isoquant, it shows you all the points of the same pressure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So you can be here or you can be in Denver and the air pressure can be the same if you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: in the same weather unit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So you just draw a cell that links together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Well, they do the same thing with utility and say lots of bananas and very few coconuts

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: can give you the same utility as lots of coconuts and very few bananas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And you draw basically like a hyperbola running down and linking the two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And they'll say, well, that's your utility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: That describes your tastes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And then we have your income.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And given your income, you can buy that many bananas completely or that many coconuts or

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: a straight line combination of the two.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And then if we double the nominal price of coconuts and double the nominal price of bananas

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: and double your income, what happens?

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And the correct answer is oh, nothing, sir.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: You stay at the same point of tangency between what your budget is and which particular utility

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: curve gives you the maximum satisfaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So that gets ingrained into them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And they think anybody who worries about money suffers from money illusion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: You were therefore ignorant of the deep insights of economics if you think money actually matters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So you have an entire theory of economics which presumes we exchange through data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Like I'll swap you that Microsoft Surface for, actually I'll take two of those for one

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: of these.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: We do this bartering type arrangement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: In fact, that only works if money plays no creative role in the economy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And that's where you'll find reading Schumpeter, the insight that's the school of thought that

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: I come from that says money is essential.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Money actually adds to demand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And we'll talk about that later on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So that's the neoclassical school that ends up being subjective theory of value, non-monetary

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: as though everything happens in barter and focusing on equilibrium as though everything

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: happens in equilibrium.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Or if you get disturbed from equilibrium, you return back to it again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And that mindset describes capitalism, its most interesting feature is that it reaches

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: equilibrium.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Now, what planet are we on to believe that because if you look at the real world, the

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: real exciting world of capitalism in which we live, change is by far the most obvious

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: characteristic of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: There's no equilibrium.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: There's no equilibrium.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: It's unstable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And as a mathematician, it's easy to, you work with stability analysis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: You work out what the Jacobian is, you work out your Lyapunov exponents in a complex system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: You're used to the idea that equilibrium is unstable, but economists get schooled in believing

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: that everything happens in equilibrium and they don't learn stability analysis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So all that stuff is missing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So onto the schools of thought, treating the economy as an equilibrium system, which was

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: what the neoclassical school did, is what Keynes disturbed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And he really disturbed it by talking about fundamentally that uncertainty determines

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: our decisions about the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So when we consume, you know, you know, if you like Vizor or whatever particular drink

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: we want to have, you know the current situation, but to invest, you must be making guesses

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: about the future, but you don't know the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So what do you do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: You extrapolate what you currently know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And this is a terrible basis on which to plan for the future, but this is the only thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: you can do where there is no possibility of solid calculation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So investment is therefore subject to uncertainty and therefore you will get volatility out

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: of investment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: You will get fads, of course, booms and slumps coming out of that because people extrapolate

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: for the current conditions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And that's the normal state of a capitalist economy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And Schumpeter argued that that's what gives us this creativity as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: The fact that you can perceive a potential demand, but you don't, first of all, you

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: don't know whether that demand is going to work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Secondly, you don't know who your competitor is going to be, whether somebody is going

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: to be ahead of you or behind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: If there's a fad, you'll over invest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: All this stuff is the real nature of capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And that's what we're trying to capture, the dynamic non-equilibrium monetary violence

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: and creativity of capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: That's what we should be analyzing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And the post-Keynesian school has gone in that orientation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: They've been, in my opinion, inhibited by learning their mathematics from neoclassical

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: economists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: So they don't have enough of the technology of complex systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: There's only a really tiny handful of people working in complex systems analysis in post-Keynesian

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: economics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And then neoclassical is value comes from like bananas and coconuts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Human preference is like human happiness, how happy a banana makes you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And then the Keynesian and the post-Keynesian were like, yeah, well, you can't, you can

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: never, the moment you try to put value to a banana and a coconut, you're already working

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: in the past.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: It's always going to be chaos and stability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303

body.input: And then you just, you're fishing in uncertain waters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steve Keen: Marxism, Capitalism, and Economics | Lex Fridman Podcast #303
